children.translated_text: Here the purpose is stated.

children.text: amaṅgalakhyāpanārthaṃ akāro ceti prayonanadvayaṃ vāsaḥpratiṣedhe draṣṭavgam
children.translated_text: For the purpose of indicating inauspiciousness, and because of the letter a: thus a twofold purpose should be seen in the prohibition of clothing.
It occurs.

children.text: hitārtham akhilaṃ yena sṛṣṭaṃ brahmādikaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: By whom the whole world, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, was created for the sake of welfare,
having bowed with the head to that <s>Paśupati</s>, the lord of the assembly,
endowed with an excellence of meaning, supreme through an excellence of knowledge,
the commentary on the five topics is composed by <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> in due order.
Someone says: the Blessed One will teach the five topics.
Now what is its opening sūtra?

children.text: atrocyate athātaḥ paśupateḥ pāśupataṃ yogavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Here it is said: "Now, therefore, we shall explain the <s>Pāśupata</s> rule of yoga belonging to <s>Paśupati</s>."
This first sūtra is recited at the beginning of the treatise.
After that, the analysis of the words is made.
"We shall explain the useful rule of yoga": such is the construction.
The sūtra consists of eight words.

children.text: tatra atha ataḥ iti dve pade naipātike ||
children.translated_text: Therein, "now" and "therefore" are two indeclinable words.
The word "of <s>Paśupati</s>" is uttered with the sense of inclusion.
"Pāśupata" is a derivative formation.
"Rule of yoga" is a compound expression.
"vi" and "āṅ" are two words.
"We shall explain" is a finite verbal form.
Someone asks: for what purpose is the analysis of the words made?
That is answered: for the sake of establishing the meaning.
Why would the meanings of the words not be established?
Because here the words have separate meanings.
For this very reason he says as follows.
Just as a man, though his body is uncovered, when covered on the head
does not become manifest, so a sūtra without analysis does not become manifest.
Thus the analysis of the words is made for the sake of establishing the meaning.
Someone says: the word analysis and its purpose have been stated.

children.text: idaṃ tu vācyam atha śāstrādiḥ kaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: But this must be stated: what is the beginning of the treatise?

children.text: atrocyate athātaḥ paśupater ity eṣa tāvacchāstrādiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here it is said: "Now, therefore, of <s>Paśupati</s>" is, first of all, the beginning of the treatise.

children.text: tatra śāstraṃ tantraṃ grantho vidyā ca ||
children.translated_text: Therein, "treatise" means system, book, and science.
Because it is a means for understanding both the book and its meaning.
Its measure is the teaching beginning with the word atha and ending with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: saṃkhyā pañcādhyāyāḥ pañca brahmāṇi adhikaraṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Its number is five chapters, five Brahmans, and the section.
From the word atha, the word ataḥ, the statement of explanation, and the instruction about bathing, lying down, and so forth, the recognition of pupil and teacher is established.

children.text: kaivalyagatānām api duḥkhitvadarśanāt kāryakāraṇapratyakṣadarśī vipratvād upāyopeyapratyakṣadarśitvāc ca praśnaprativaktā aiśvaryāvasthaś caiva muktatvān mano'manaḥsaṃsthaś ca kāmitvād ataḥ sarvācāryaviśiṣṭo 'yam ācārya iti ||
children.translated_text: Because even those who have attained isolation are seen to suffer; because he directly perceives effect and cause, is a Brahmin, and directly perceives both means and goal, he is the question-answerer, established in lordly power, liberated, abiding in mind and no-mind, and, because he is possessed of will, this teacher is superior to all teachers.

children.text: tathā brāhmaṇagrahaṇāt strīpratiṣedhād indriyajayopadeśāc ca uktaṃ hi
children.translated_text: Likewise, because a Brahmin is specified, because women are excluded, and because conquest of the senses is taught, it has been said:

children.text: bādhiryam āndhyam aghratvaṃ mūkatā jaḍatā tathā
children.translated_text: Deafness, blindness, lack of smell, muteness, dullness likewise,
madness, crookedness, leprosy, impotence, obstruction of the rectum, and lameness:
free from these and having keen senses, the Brahmin is the pupil.
And he is a pupil superior to others.

children.text: tathā devādibhyaś ca krīḍādharmitvāt krīḍānimittā īśvarapravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in relation to the gods and others, since play is his nature, the activity of the Lord has play as its cause.
And the teacher's activity in speaking the teaching is for the sake of grace.
Likewise, because of instruction concerning worship, prompting, grace, and the desire for becoming <s>Śiva</s>, the pupil who seeks the end of suffering undertakes approach here.
But he is not here for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, or isolation.

children.text: tathā kāmitvād indrakauśikādibhyaś cācāryo divyo niratiśayakrīḍaiśvaryasvābhāvyād ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, because he possesses will, and in comparison with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and others, the teacher is divine, by reason of the naturalness of unsurpassed play and lordly power: this is the meaning.

children.text: codanopasadanasaṃskāravaśyādiduḥkhair abhibhūtatvāc cādivyā indrakauśikādyāḥ śiṣyā iti ||
children.translated_text: And because they are overcome by sufferings due to injunction, approach, consecration, subjection, and so on, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and the others are non-divine pupils.

children.text: tathā śiṣṭaprāmāṇyāt kāmitvād ajātatvāc ca manuṣyarūpī bhagavān brāhmaṇakāyam āsthāya kāyāvataraṇe avatīrṇa iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, on the authority of the learned, because he possesses will and because he is unborn, the Blessed One, assuming human form and taking on a Brahmin body, descended in the descent into a body.
Likewise, he reached <s>Ujjayinī</s> on foot.
Why?
Because of the authority of the learned and because signs have been seen and heard.

children.text: atyāśramaprasiddhaṃ liṅgamāsthāya pravacanam uktavān bhasmasnānaśayanānusnānanirmālyaikavāsograhaṇād adhikaraṇaprasiddhyarthaṃ ca svaśāstrokte āyatane śiṣyasambandhārthaṃ śucau deśe bhasmavedyāmuṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking up the emblem known among those beyond the āśramas, he spoke the teaching; for the sake of establishing the section through ash-bathing, lying on ashes, repeated bathing, taking remnants, and one garment, and for the sake of connection with the pupil, he stayed in a pure place, on an ash-altar, in the sanctuary taught in his own scripture.

children.text: ato rudrapracoditaḥ kuśikabhagavān abhyāgatyācārye paripūrṇaparitṛptyādyutkarṣalakṣaṇāni viparītāni cātmani dṛṣṭvā pādāv upasaṃgṛhya nyāyena jātiṃ gotraṃ śrutam anṛṇatvaṃ ca nivedayitvā kṛtakṣaṇam ācāryaṃ kāle vaidyavad avasthitam āturavad avasthitaḥ śiṣyaḥ pṛṣṭavān bhagavan kim eteṣām ādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikānāṃ sarvaduḥkhānām aikāntiko 'tyantiko vyapoho 'sty uta neti
children.translated_text: Then, impelled by <s>Rudra</s>, the blessed <s>Kuśika</s> came; seeing in the teacher the marks of excellence such as complete satisfaction and fullness, and seeing the opposite marks in himself, he clasped the feet, duly declared his birth, lineage, learning, and freedom from debt, and, like a patient approaching a physician at the right time, asked the teacher, who had made the proper occasion and was rightly situated: "Blessed one, is there an absolute and final removal of all these sufferings, internal, material, and divine, or is there not?"

children.text: athoktaparigrahādhikāralipsāsu parāpadeśenopadeśe sacchiṣyasādhakapāṭhaprasiddhyarthaṃ kāraṇapadārthādhigamārthaṃ cātmani parāpadeśaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān evoktavān atheti
children.translated_text: Then, wishing for the eligibility belonging to the accepted matter previously stated, and in order that instruction by indirect designation, the reading concerning the true pupil and practitioner, and the understanding of the causal category might become established, the Blessed One, making an indirect designation with reference to himself, himself uttered "atha."
Here, when there is dependence on what has been introduced before, the word atha is used.
How so?
In dependence on the question previously uttered by the pupil, he said "atha."
Thus this word atha has the meaning of a reply to what has been asked.
That means the end of suffering.

children.text: āha kiṃ parīkṣitāya śiṣyāya duḥkhāntaḥ pratijñātaḥ utāparīkṣitāyeti
children.translated_text: He says: Is the end of suffering promised to a disciple who has been examined, or to one who has not been examined?
It is said: to one who has been examined.
For he says, "therefore."
Here the word "therefore" expresses the qualities of the disciple.

children.text: yasmād ayaṃ brahmāvartadeśajaḥ kulajaḥ paṭvindriyo vividiṣādisampannaḥ śiṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: For this disciple is born in the land of <s>Brahmāvarta</s>, born in a good family, has keen senses, and is endowed with the desire to know and the other qualifications.
And earlier too, the word "therefore" should here be understood according to the sense.

children.text: atha sa duḥkhāntaḥ kutaḥ prāpyate kena vābhyupāyeneti
children.translated_text: Now, from where is that end of suffering obtained, or by what means?
That is stated: from <s>Paśupati</s>.
"Through grace" is the completion of the sentence.
Here, he is the lord of the <s>paśus</s>.
He is <s>Paśupati</s>.

children.text: atra paśavo nāma siddheśvaravarjaṃ sarve cetanāvantaḥ
children.translated_text: Here the <s>paśus</s> are all sentient beings except the perfected lords.
The <s>paśus</s> are those colored by effect and instrument, and also those without such coloring.
He says: What is their condition of being <s>paśus</s>?
It is said: lack of lordship is bondage.
Lack of autonomy, characterized by the obstruction of causal power, is lack of lordship; bondage is beginningless.
It is figuratively called a quality of bondage.
If one asks, "What is its characteristic?"

children.text: tad ucyate paśyanāt pāśanāc ca paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: that is stated: they are <s>paśus</s> because they see and because they are bound.
There the <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) are the <s>kalās</s> called effect and instrument.
And we shall explain those <s>kalās</s> later.

children.text: tābhiḥ pāśitāḥ baddhāḥ saṃniruddhāḥ śabdādiviṣayaparavaśāś ca bhūtvāvatiṣṭhante ity ato 'vagamyate 'svātantryam anaiśvaryaṃ bandhaḥ
children.translated_text: Bound, tied, and restrained by them, and having become dependent on objects such as sound, they remain in that state; therefore lack of autonomy, lack of lordship, and bondage are understood.
If it is said that the condition of being a <s>paśu</s> ceases for one who is without effect and instrument,

children.text: tad ucyate saṃhṛtānām api punaḥ punaḥ saṃbandhagrahaṇācchāstre
children.translated_text: that is answered: because scripture states that even when they have been withdrawn, they repeatedly take on connection again.
What else?
They are also <s>paśus</s> because they see.

children.text: yasmād vibhutve 'pi citsamavetatve 'pi ca śarīramātram eva paśyanty upalabhanti ca na bahirddhāni
children.translated_text: For although they are pervasive and although they are joined with consciousness, they see and perceive only the body, not what lies outside.

children.text: kāryakaraṇarahitāś ca na kāryakaraṇaṃ pratipadyate tyajanti vā
children.translated_text: And when they are without effect and instrument, they neither take up nor abandon effect and instrument.
This is because they depend on <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, manifestation, place, time, prompting, and so on.

children.text: ataḥ suṣṭhūktaṃ paśyanāt pāśanāc ca paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore it has been well said: they are <s>paśus</s> because they see and because they are bound.

children.text: yasmād uktaṃ sāṃkhyayogena ye muktāḥ sāṃkhyayogeśvarāś ca ye
children.translated_text: For it has been said: those who are liberated by <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s>, and those who are lords of <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s>,

children.text: brahmādayas tiryagantāḥ sarve te paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Brahmā</s> down to animals, all of them are remembered as <s>paśus</s>.
Why is he called <s>pati</s> (lord)?

children.text: āpti pāti ca tān paśūn ity ataḥ patir bhavati
children.translated_text: Because he reaches and protects those <s>paśus</s>; therefore he becomes their lord.
By what does he reach them, and by what does he protect them?
Therefore, by the power of pervasion.
For even there they do not pass beyond his infinite power.
And because of his distinct superiority, his power of knowledge is infinite and immeasurable.

children.text: tayā aparimitayā aparimitān eva pratyakṣān paśūn āpnotīti patiḥ
children.translated_text: By that immeasurable power he reaches the immeasurable <s>paśus</s> directly; therefore he is the lord.
Likewise, because he protects them, this is his lordly power.
Why?
Because by his command their activity and cessation, their stability, and their attainment of desired and undesired places, bodies, senses, objects, and the like take place.
The meaning is: they are seen by him and impelled by him.
Thus.
In the expression "of <s>Paśupati</s>," effect, cause, and also grace are indicated.
From that grace, that end of suffering is obtained.
The meaning is that it is not obtained merely from knowledge, dispassion, <s>dharma</s>, lordship, or renunciation.

children.text: āha kutrasthasya kadā kīdṛśasya vā sa bhagavān prasīdatīti
children.translated_text: He says: Where situated, when, or being of what kind, does that blessed one become gracious?

children.text: ucyate yadānena tu tat prāptaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: It is said: when this has been obtained by him.
He says: What is that?

children.text: ucyate pāśupatam atra paśupatinoktaṃ parigṛhītaṃ paśupatim adhikṛtya cārabhyata iti pāśupatam
children.translated_text: It is said: <s>Pāśupata</s>. Here, because it is taught by <s>Paśupati</s>, accepted by him, and begun with reference to <s>Paśupati</s>, it is called <s>Pāśupata</s>.
As in the expressions "<s>Vaiṣṇava</s>" and "<s>Mānasa</s>."
What is that?
It is yoga.
Here yoga is the conjunction of the self and the Lord.
Again, because for a person it has causes such as study, it is produced by the action of one or the other, like the post and the hawk.
Because injunction, study, and the like are taught, it is produced by the action of both, like a ram.
For even though there is pervasiveness, separation is not produced by authority.
And conjunction is taught only for one who is separated.
This is as in action-yoga, like one attached to or detached from an object.

children.text: iha tu samādhilakṣaṇe yoge saṃniyama iti
children.translated_text: Here, however, in yoga characterized by samādhi, it is restraint.

children.text: āha kiṃ parijñānamātrād eva tadyogaḥ prāpyate
children.translated_text: He says: Is that yoga obtained merely from complete knowledge?
It is said:
because he says, "We shall explain the method for attaining that."

children.text: atra yogasya vidhiḥ yogavidhir iti ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣasamāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Here "the method of yoga" is a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, "yoga-method."
Here the term "method" applies to subtle and gross, external and internal, similar and dissimilar actions, as in the method of a sacrifice.
But not as in compounds such as "army and forest."
Why?
Because momentary actions cannot form a collective whole.
If that is so, why is it called a method?
It is a method because it enjoins.
And also because there is a relation of means and end.
The word "method" is the object.

children.text: eva saduḥkhāntaḥ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ yogo vidhir iti pañcaiva padārthāḥ samāsata uddiṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the end of suffering, effect, cause, yoga, and method are precisely the five topics briefly set forth.
They are to be explained.
The explanation of these consists of expansion, division, specification, summing up, and final statement.
Therefore the thing to be explained is one thing, and the explanation is another.
For he says, "We shall explain."

children.text: atra viḥ vistare vibhāge viśeṣe ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Here the prefix <s>vi</s> has the senses of expansion, division, and specification.
There, "expansion" refers to perception, inference,
and trustworthy testimony; these are called means of knowledge.

children.text: tatra pratyakṣaṃ dvividham indriyapratyakṣam ātmapratyakṣaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Among them, perception is twofold: perception by the senses and perception by the self.
Sense-perception is established by sense-objects: sound, touch, form, taste, smell, pot and food, and by explanation, heat, urine, feces, flesh, salt, and breath-control.
Self-perception is established from the statement about that which brings the whole offering, austerity, the end of suffering, and the like.
Just as rice measured by a <s>prastha</s> is called a <s>prastha</s>.

But in the highest sense a true <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) arises when the complex of factors that reveals the relation between sense-organ and object is assisted by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, illumination, place, time, prompting, and the like.
Self-perception, however, has as its complex of conditions the connection of consciousness, the inner instrument, and the self.

children.text: anumānam api pratyakṣapūrvakaṃ cittātmāntaḥkaraṇasambandhasāmagryaṃ ca dharmādharmaprakāśadeśakālacodanādismṛtihetukam utpattyanugrahatirobhāvakālādi
children.translated_text: Inference too, preceded by perception, has as its complex of conditions the connection of consciousness, self, and inner instrument; and its production is assisted, concealed, timed, and so on by memory whose causes are <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, illumination, place, time, prompting, and the like.
And by these the causative agent's making of the subsequent creation is inferred.
Therefore it is not outside the sūtra.

children.text: tac ca dvividhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And that is of two kinds: what is seen and what is seen in a general way.

children.text: tatra dṛṣṭam api dvividhaṃ pūrvavaccheṣavac ca
children.translated_text: There too, what is seen is also of two kinds: like the former and like the remainder.

children.text: tatra pūrvadṛṣṭo 'yaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulīyakaḥ sa eveti pūrvavat
children.translated_text: For example, 'This is the same man with six fingers who was seen before': this is like the former.
From seeing only horns and the like, one says, 'It is a cow': this is like the remainder.

children.text: sāmānyatodṛṣṭam apīha gatipūrvikāṃ deśāntaraprāptiṃ dṛṣṭvā cāsyādityādigatiprasiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: What is seen in a general way is illustrated here: after seeing arrival in another place preceded by motion, one establishes motion in the sun and the like.
A <s>pramāṇa</s> is the cause for the apprehension of an object, even in relation to the three times.

children.text: āgamo nāma ā maheśvarād gurupāramparyāgataṃ śāstram
children.translated_text: <s>Āgama</s> is the scripture that has come down from <s>Maheśvara</s> through the succession of teachers.
<s>Āgama</s> is taught and remembered as the cause of dealings concerning what is non-worldly and so forth.
<s>Rudra</s> declared it; from his word comes attainment.
The inclusion of comparison, postulation, possibility, absence, tradition, intuition, and the like, when they are explained, is within these very means.
Thus these are the three <s>pramāṇas</s>.
The one who causes knowledge is the blessed Lord, the prompter.
The knower is the person.
The knowables are the five categories, beginning with effect and cause.
Cognition is awareness.

children.text: saṃvit saṃcintanaṃ sambodho vidyābhivyaktir ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: Awareness means reflection, awakening, knowledge, and manifestation.
And from indication, specification, and understanding, the syllable 'vi' has the sense of extension.
Division means the non-confusion of words, meanings, sūtras, sections, chapters, and so forth.
Specificity means the distinction between what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment.
'Āṅ' has the sense of the limit of explanation.

children.text: padāt padaṃ sūtrāt sūtraṃ prakaraṇāt prakaraṇam adhyāyād adhyāyam ā bodhād ā parisamāpter iti maryādāvasthasyaiva ca vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall speak only within that limit: from word to word, from sūtra to sūtra, from section to section, from chapter to chapter, up to understanding and up to completion.
The root 'khyā' means proclamation.
We shall explain by means of terms already understood and not yet understood, and apart from what is laid down in the Veda and other sources.
'Syā' refers to future time.

children.text: yāvad ayam ācāryo gṛhasthādibhyo 'bhyāgataṃ pūrvam ataḥśabdāt parīkṣitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vratopavāsādyaṃ mahādevasya dakṣiṇasyāṃ mūrtai sadyojātādisaṃskṛtena bhasmanā saṃskaroti utpattiliṅgavyāvṛttiṃ kṛtvā mantraśrāvaṇaṃ ca karoti tāvad eṣyaḥ kālaḥ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: As long as this teacher consecrates, with ash consecrated by the <s>Sadyojāta</s> and other mantras in the southern form of <s>Mahādeva</s>, the Brāhmaṇa who has come first to householders and others, who has been examined according to the preceding word 'ataḥ', and who is marked by vows, fasts, and so on, and as long as he removes the distinction marked by birth and causes the mantra to be heard, so long is the future time being indicated.
'Ma' has the sense of a proposition.

children.text: utthānādigaṇe samyagvvāvasthitasya vyākhyeyavyākhyānayor bhagavān eva kramaśo vaktā ||
children.translated_text: For one who is properly established in the group beginning with rising, the blessed Lord himself is, in sequence, the speaker both of what is to be explained and of the explanation.

children.text: sthūlopāyapūrvakatvāt sūkṣmavidheyādhigamasya pūrvāśramaniyamapratiṣedhārtham atyāśramayamaniyamaprasiddhyarthaṃ ca vidhiḥ prathamaṃ vyākhyāyate ||
children.translated_text: Since the understanding of what is subtle and enjoined depends on a gross means, the rule is explained first in order to prohibit the restrictions of the former āśramas and to establish the yamas and niyamas of the state beyond the āśramas.
Here the presentation of the topic is completed.
Here someone says: 'The part already accepted is explained first according to rule.'
This is now to be considered.

children.text: athāsya kaś cādiḥ kiṃ madhyaṃ ko 'ntaḥ katyaṅgo vā vidhir iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, what is the beginning of this rule, what is its middle, what is its end, and how many limbs does it have?

children.text: tad ucyate bhasmanādyo nindāmadhyo mūḍhāntaś ca vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is answered: the rule has ash as its beginning, censure as its middle, and the deluded as its end.
And it has three limbs: giving, sacrificing, and austerity.

children.text: tat katham avagamyate yasmād idam ārabhyate ||
children.translated_text: How is that understood? Because this is begun.

children.text: atra bhasma vāmadravyaṃ yad agnīndhanasaṃyogān niṣpannam ||
children.translated_text: Here ash is a left-hand substance, produced from the conjunction of fire and fuel.
It is made by another, earthy, consumed, and luminous.
Ash should be collected from villages and the like, as alms are collected.

children.text: snānaśayanānusnānakṛtyabandhutvān niṣparigrahatvād ahiṃsakatvād utkṛṣṭam eva śuci prabhūtaṃ grāhyaṃ sādhanatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Because it is connected with the acts of bathing, lying down, and bathing again, because it involves possessionlessness, and because it is harmless, one should take only what is excellent, pure, and abundant, since it is an instrument.
If that is not available, even a little should be taken.
A receptacle too, such as a gourd, hide, or cloth, is well known in this context.
Someone asks: 'What is to be done with that ash?'

children.text: tad ucyate bhasmaneti tṛtīyā karaṇārthe kartuḥ kriyām ādiśati yathā vāśyā takṣaṇaṃ buddhyā pidhānam ||
children.translated_text: The answer is this: in 'with ash', the third case-ending has the sense of an instrument and enjoins the agent's action, just as cutting is done with an axe and covering with the intellect.

children.text: āha atha kasmin kāle sā kriyā kartavyeti ||
children.translated_text: Someone asks: 'Then at what time is that action to be performed?'
'At the three pressings.'
This is a dvigu compound.
'Three' is the number.
'Pressing' is the designation of the time.
The three twilights are the morning twilight, the midday twilight, and the evening twilight.
'At the three pressings' means at the three twilights, at the three times.
Someone asks: 'What is to be done at the three pressings?'
The answer is: 'One should bathe.'

children.text: atra snānaṃ śaucakāryeṇa śarīreṣv āgantukānāṃ snehatvaglepamalagandhādīnāṃ bhasmanāpakarṣaṇaṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Here bathing means that, for the sake of purity, the accidental oiliness, skin-smearing, dirt, odor, and the like on the bodies should be removed with ash.
Bathing, moreover, is the joining of the ash-substance with the limbs.

children.text: paramārthatas tu snānādi puṇyaphalasaṃyogadharmātmavacanād ātmaśaucam evaitat ||
children.translated_text: But in the highest sense, since bathing and the rest are spoken of as a property of the self connected with the fruit of merit, this is simply purification of the self.
It is only because of statements such as 'by bathing and the rest one becomes stainless, rid of sin, and so on' that purification of the self is explained by the designation of action and instrument.

children.text: ita ity etad ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca ||
children.translated_text: 'Ita' indicates command and injunction.

children.text: niyogatvān nigataṃ niyatatvān nigama ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it is an injunction, it is called nigata; because it is fixed, it is called nigama: this is the meaning.
Why?
Because it is established within its own system, because it is harmless, and because it is a cause of the highest good.

children.text: bhasmanā sneyaṃ na cādbhir viparītatvād ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should bathe with ash, not with waters, because that would be the opposite: this is the meaning.
Is bathing itself alone to be performed in this way with ash?
The answer is given.
For he says:
Here 'ash' is just that same ash.
Its etymological explanation was stated before.
In 'in ash', the locative denotes close contact and proximity.
'One should lie' is the designation of quieting down and resting.

children.text: ita ity etad ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca ||
children.translated_text: The word 'ita' here has the sense of command and injunction.

children.text: bhasmany eva rātrau svaptavyaṃ nānyatrety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should sleep at night only in ash, not elsewhere: this is the meaning.
For it has been said:

children.text: yathā mṛgā mṛtyubhayasya bhītā udvignavāsā na labhanti nidrām
children.translated_text: Just as deer, afraid from fear of death, living in alarm, do not find sleep,

children.text: evaṃ yatir dhyānaparo mahātmā saṃsārabhīto na labheta nidrām ||
children.translated_text: so the great-souled ascetic, intent on meditation and afraid of saṃsāra, should not find sleep.
Moreover, because he seeks something special.
And this Brāhmaṇa is one who seeks something special.
For it has been said:

children.text: na viśeṣārthināṃ nidrā ciraṃ netreṣu tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Sleep does not remain long in the eyes of those who seek something special,
like well-bred horses that lie down for half of midnight or half the night.

children.text: tasmāt parivṛṣṭe bhūpradeśe divā parigrahaṃ kṛtvā bhasmāstīryādhyayanādhyāpanadhyānābhiniviṣṭena pravacanacintanābhiniveśaiś ca śrāntena bāhūpadhānena sadyojātādisaṃskṛte bhasmani rātrau svaptavyam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, on a piece of ground that has been sprinkled all around, after taking possession of it by day, one should spread ash and sleep at night in ash consecrated with the <s>Sadyojāta</s> and other mantras, using the arms as a pillow, after becoming absorbed in study, teaching, and meditation, and after growing weary through devotion to recitation and reflection: this is the meaning.
If one asks, 'For what purpose?',

children.text: ucyate tapo'rthaṃ bhūpradeśe śaucārthaṃ viśrāmārthaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: the answer is: for the sake of austerity on the ground, for the sake of purity, or for the sake of rest.

children.text: samaviṣamanimnonnatāyāṃ bhūmau yāmaṃ yāmadvayaṃ vā svaptavyam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should sleep for one watch or two watches on ground that is level and uneven, low and high: this is the meaning.

children.text: āha kiṃ snānaṃ śayanaṃ ca bhasmanā prayojanadvayam evātra kartavyam utānyad api ||
children.translated_text: Someone says: 'Are bathing and lying down with ash alone the two purposes to be performed here, or is there something else as well?'
'What removes the impurity that befalls this person while he remains between the three pressings?'
That is answered.
As in bathing with mantras and the like.
Here anu has the sense of an action performed afterward.
As in drinking afterward and following after.
But bathing is simply the application of the ash-substance.

children.text: savanatraye snānasyāntareṣu bhuktocchiṣṭakṣutaniṣṭhīvitamūtrapurīṣotsargādinimittakam aśaucakam abhisamīkṣya tad anusnānaṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Between the bathings at the three pressings, when one observes impurity caused by such things as eating remnants, sneezing, spitting, urination, defecation, and the like, that subsequent bathing should be performed.

children.text: kimartham iti cet śaucārthaṃ liṅgābhivyaktyarthaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: If one asks, 'For what purpose?', it is for the sake of purity and for the manifestation of the <s>liṅga</s> (mark).
It means 'one should bathe.'
Someone says: 'Is ash alone the cause of the manifestation of the <s>liṅga</s>?'

children.text: bhaktivivṛddhau vā apratiṣiddhasya sādhanaṃ kim iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Or, for the increase of devotion, what is the means that is not prohibited?'
That is answered.
Here, like ash, <s>nirmālya</s> is well known among people and so forth.
Nir is the designation of what has been released or removed.
Mālya is a synonym for a collection of flowers.
That means lotus, blue lotus, and the like, made by another, placed upon and then taken down from the causal form, and free from possession.

children.text: bhaktivivṛddhyarthaṃ liṅgābhivyaktyarthaṃ ca tad dhāryam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be worn for the increase of devotion and for the manifestation of the <s>liṅga</s>: this is the meaning.

children.text: āha bhasmanirmālyena tasya liṅgaṃ vyaktaṃ bhavatīti kva siddham ||
children.translated_text: Someone says: 'Where is it established that his <s>liṅga</s> becomes manifest through ash and <s>nirmālya</s>?'
That is answered here.
For he says:

children.text: atra yathānyeṣām api varṇāśramiṇām āśramaprativibhāgakarāṇi liṅgāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Here, just as members of other social classes and āśramas also have marks that distinguish the divisions of āśrama,

children.text: tatra gṛhasthasya tāvad vāsas trayaṃ vaiṇavī yaṣṭiḥ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalu sottaroṣṭhavapanaṃ yajñopavītādi liṅgam ||
children.translated_text: there, first, the marks of a householder are three garments, a bamboo staff, a water-filled water-pot, shaving of the upper lip, the sacred thread, and so on.
Likewise, the marks of a brahmacārin are a staff, water-pot, muñja grass girdle, sacred thread, black antelope skin, and so on.
Likewise, the marks of a forest-dweller are the wearing of karīra cloth, bark garments, a moustache or beard, matted hair, and so on.
Likewise, the marks of a mendicant are the triple staff, shaven head, water-pot, ochre robe, water-strainer, earth-strainer, and so on.

children.text: evam ihāpi yad etat pāśupatayogādhikaraṇaṃ liṅgam ity āśramaprativibhāgakaraṃ bhasmasnānaśayanānusnānanirmālyaikavāsādiniṣpannaṃ svaśarīralīnaṃ pāśupatam iti laukikādijñānajanakaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: So here too, this mark connected with Pāśupata yoga, distinguishing the divisions of āśrama, produced by bathing in ash, lying in ash, subsequent bathing, <s>nirmālya</s>, a single garment, and the like, merged into one's own body, and generating ordinary and other knowledge that 'this person is a <s>Pāśupata</s>,' is that <s>liṅga</s>.
It is called <s>liṅga</s> both because of merging and because it indicates.
By bearing that, one becomes a bearer of the <s>liṅga</s>.
It is like one who bears a staff: this is the meaning.
Someone says: 'Now where should these matters, bathing, lying down, subsequent bathing, and the like, be performed?'
'And from where should the <s>nirmālya</s> be obtained?'
'Or while staying where should it be worn?'
'And where should one who has made the <s>liṅga</s> dwell?'
That is answered: in an <s>āyatana</s> (sacred precinct).
For he says:
Now the <s>āyatana</s>, like ash and <s>nirmālya</s>, is well known among people.
The particle āṅ has the sense of a boundary.

children.text: yasmād ete gṛhasthādayaḥ prayataniyataśucisādhvācārāḥ svasvamaryādayopatiṣṭhante yajanti ca śāntikapauṣṭikādibhiḥ kriyābhir iti ||
children.translated_text: Because householders and the others, being careful, restrained, pure, and of good conduct, attend and worship according to their own respective boundaries, with rites for pacification, prosperity, and the like.
And because of worship, it is called an <s>āyatana</s>.

children.text: tasmin parakṛta āyatane vastavyam iti vāsī ity āyatanaṃ ca parigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: In that <s>āyatana</s> made by another one should dwell; thus, as a dweller, he also accepts the <s>āyatana</s>.

children.text: bhūpradeśe ākāśe vṛkṣamūle bahiḥ prādakṣiṇyena vā yatra kvacit prativasan śiṣṭamaryādayā āyatanavāsī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: While residing anywhere, on a piece of ground, in the open air, at the root of a tree, outside, or to the right in circumambulation, he becomes a dweller in an <s>āyatana</s> according to the boundary observed by the learned.
It means that he should dwell as one dwelling on a riverbank dwells.
And the attainment of the fruit of merit comes to him quickly.
For it has been said:

children.text: grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyasthānaṃ hi śūlinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether in a village or in a forest, it is indeed a meritorious place of <s>Śūlin</s>.

children.text: āvāso dharmatṛptānāṃ siddhikṣetraṃ hi tat param ||
children.translated_text: For that supreme place is the field of attainment for those who are satisfied by <s>dharma</s> (religious discipline).

children.text: āha tasmin āyatane prativasatā kāḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He asks: while residing in that shrine, what actions are to be performed?
Are they bathing and the like, or smearing and the like?

children.text: āhosvid dṛṣṭā asyānyā vaiśeṣikyaḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or are there other special actions prescribed for him, as seen in tradition?

children.text: yathā cānyā vaiśeṣikyaḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ prayojanaṃ ca vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since other special actions are to be performed, we shall state their purpose as well.

children.text: atha triṣu snānakāleṣu sadyojātādisaṃskṛtena bhasmanā japatā snātvā japataivāyatanam abhigantavyam ||
children.translated_text: Now, at the three times for bathing, having bathed while reciting, with ash consecrated by the <s>Sadyojāta</s> and other mantras, one should approach the shrine while reciting.

children.text: abhigamya ca yat pūrvaṃ japati tat pratyāhārārthaṃ japyam oṃ oṃ oṃ ||
children.translated_text: And having approached, what he recites first is to be recited for the sake of <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal): oṃ, oṃ, oṃ.

children.text: hasitādīni tu kṛtvā yat paścāj japati tanniyamārthaṃ japyam ||
children.translated_text: But after performing laughter and the other actions, what he recites afterward is to be recited for the sake of the rule.

children.text: tad atra hasitaṃ nāma yad etat kaṇṭhauṣṭhapuṭavisphūrjanam aṭṭahāsaḥ kriyate taddhasitam ||
children.translated_text: Here, what is called laughter is this bursting forth from the throat and the cavity of the lips, the loud laugh that is made; that is laughter.

children.text: gītam api gāndharvaśāstrasamayānabhiṣvaṅgeṇa yatra bhagavato maheśvarasya sabhāyāṃ gauṇadravyajakarmajāni nāmāni cintyante tat ||
children.translated_text: Song too is that in which, without attachment to the conventions of <s>Gāndharvaśāstra</s>, the names of the blessed <s>Maheśvara</s>, arising from qualities, substances, and actions, are contemplated in his assembly.

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ prākṛtaṃ parakṛtam ātmakṛtaṃ vā yad gīyate tad geyam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is sung, whether in Sanskrit, Prakrit, composed by another, or composed by oneself, is what is to be sung.

children.text: nṛttam api nāṭyaśāstrasamayānabhiṣvaṅgeṇa hastapādādīnām utkṣepaṇam avakṣepaṇam ākuñcanaṃ prasāraṇaṃ calanam anavasthānam ||
children.translated_text: Dance too, without attachment to the conventions of <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>, is the raising, lowering, bending, extending, moving, and not remaining still of the hands, feet, and so on.
At the time of conclusion, dance accompanied by song should be employed for the sake of the rule.

children.text: ḍuṃḍuṃkāro nāma ya eṣa jihvāgratālusaṃyogān niṣpadyate puṇyo vṛṣanādasadṛśaḥ saḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ḍuṃḍuṃ-sound is that sacred sound, like the bellow of a bull, which is produced from the contact of the tip of the tongue with the palate.
The making of ḍuṃḍuṃ is the ḍuṃḍuṃ-sound.
The word kāra is for determining that the ḍuṃḍuṃ-sound is a limb of the offering.
The word nama, thus.
It should be made neither with the lips nor in a whisper.
But mental bowing is <s>namaskāra</s> (salutation).
The word kāra means the prohibition of vocal and whispered forms, and also the determination that it is a limb of the mental offering.

children.text: japyaṃ nāma sadyojātādiṣv akṣarapaṅktyāṃ manasā bhāvasya saṃcāravicāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Japa</s> (recitation) is the mental movement and reflection of the intention through the row of syllables beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
That is <s>japa</s>.
The prefix upa occurs in the sense of qualification, in the summing up of an action, and in totality.

children.text: upaharaṇād upahāro vrataṃ niyama ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it is an offering, <s>upahāra</s> means a vow or rule.
It is called <s>upahāra</s> because it is brought near and presented by the practitioner, who acts only through the injunction.
One should attend upon him.
Here upa has the sense of acceptance.
The meaning is: by one who has accepted, who stands within the rule, and who is bowed and bent down.
The phrase 'one should stand' concerns one-pointedness; it refers specifically to remaining in the state where <s>pratyāhāra</s> is not absent.

children.text: sarvakaraṇānāṃ vṛttau pratyāhāraṃ kṛtvā kāyikavācikamānasikābhiḥ kriyābhir upahāraṃ kṛtvā bhṛtyavad upahāreṇa stheyam ||
children.translated_text: Having made <s>pratyāhāra</s> in the activity of all the faculties, and having made an offering through bodily, verbal, and mental actions, one should remain with the offering like a servant.
The leftward and rightward circumambulations we shall explain later.
He asks: whose <s>nirmālya</s> (consecrated remnant) should be worn?
Or in whose shrine should one reside?
And where should one attend upon him?
That is stated.
Here, the word 'great' has the sense of being superior.

children.text: sarvakṣetrajñānām abhyadhika utkṛṣṭo vyatiriktaś ca bhavatīty abhyadhikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is superior because he is higher than all knowers of the field, outstanding, and distinct.
He is a seer, a learned Brahmin, and a lord.
We shall explain the state of <s>Sadāśiva</s> and superiority.
Here, the word deva is from the root divu, 'to play.'
Because play is his nature.
As heat is the nature of fire.

children.text: krīḍāvān eva bhagavān vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñakaṃ trividham api kāryam utpādayati anugṛhṇāti tirobhāvayati ca ||
children.translated_text: The blessed Lord, precisely as one who possesses play, produces the threefold effect called <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>paśu</s>, and he favors it and conceals it.
For it has been said:
The Lord, not prompted, but prompting those who are to be prompted, acting according to his will,

children.text: krīḍate bhagavān lokair bālaḥ krīḍanakair iva ||
children.translated_text: the blessed one plays with the worlds as a child plays with toys.
'Of the deva' is a genitive.
The relation is that of possession and possessor.
It refers only to the purpose of possession.
Here, the word dakṣiṇā occurs in the division of directions.
The sun divides the directions.
And the directions divide the form.

children.text: mūrtināma yad etad devasya dakṣiṇe pārśve sthitenodaṅmukhenopānte yad rūpam upalabhyate vṛṣadhvajaśūlapāṇinandimahākālordhvaliṅgādilakṣaṇaṃ yad vā laukikāḥ pratipadyante mahādevasyāyatanam iti tatropastheyam ||
children.translated_text: The form is that appearance perceived nearby on the southern side of the god, standing and facing north, marked by the bull-banner, the trident in the hand, <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, the raised <s>liṅga</s>, and so on; or else it is what ordinary people understand as the shrine of <s>Mahādeva</s>. There one should attend upon him.
Because the southern form is mentioned, the eastern, northern, and western forms are prohibited.
And because the form is prescribed, when there is no form the rule lapses.
This is the meaning: because what is obtained by begging is not to be used, and because exclusions have been stated.

children.text: vidhir ity upadiṣṭānām arthānāṃ bhasmasnānopadeśād apsu snānādīnāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the teaching of bathing with ash is among the matters prescribed as the rule, bathing in water and the like is prohibited.
Since lying on ash is taught, lying on ordinary beds and the like is prohibited.
Because the purpose of residing in a shrine is taught, other kinds of residence are prohibited.
Because laughter and the other actions are taught, the remaining offerings are prohibited.
Because <s>nirmālya</s> is taught, fresh garlands are prohibited.
Because ash, <s>nirmālya</s>, and the <s>liṅga</s> are taught, the remaining marks are prohibited.
Because <s>Mahādeva</s> is mentioned, devotion to other deities is prohibited.
Because the southern form is mentioned, the eastern and western forms are prohibited.

children.text: evaṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtir ity ukte asya brāhmaṇasya pūrvaprasiddhā niyamā niyamaiḥ pratiṣidhyante ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when 'the southern form' is stated, the previously established rules for this Brahmin are prohibited by these rules.
like a peg and counter-peg, and like old water and fresh water.
Here this section on ash is completed.
Someone says: Surely the doubt arises precisely because the niyamas have been stated.
Where there are yamas, there are niyamas.
For this is indeed a pair.
Therefore there is no doubt.
Which yamas are considered in this tantra?
The answer is: the well-known yamas, beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-injury).
But here others have a different enumeration.
Non-injury, celibacy, and truthfulness, together with non-transacting,

children.text: asteyam iti pañcaite yamā vai saṃprakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and non-stealing: these five are proclaimed as yamas.
Freedom from anger, service to the teacher, purity, lightness of diet,
and vigilance: these five are proclaimed as niyamas.
It is not so for us in that way.
Why?
Because the cessation of niyamas is observed.

children.text: asmin hi tantre kālāntaritā niyamā nivartante ||
children.translated_text: For in this tantra, niyamas separated by intervals of time come to an end.

children.text: katham ā dehapātād yamānāṃ na nivṛttir asti ||
children.translated_text: How so? Until the fall of the body there is no cessation of the yamas.
Why?
Because of the faults beginning with violence.

children.text: tasmād ahiṃsādyā daśa sarve te yamāḥ pratyavagantavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore all ten, beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s>, should be understood as yamas.

children.text: āha yady evaṃ nigamanivṛttau bhraṣṭaniyamasya patanaprasaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Someone says: If this is so, then when the rule ceases there would follow a fall for one whose niyama has lapsed.
The answer is: since its purpose has been completed, there is no consequence of falling.
Moreover, because the yamas are primary.

children.text: uktaṃ hi patati niyamavān yameṣv asakto na tu yamavān niyamālaso 'vasīdet ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said: One who possesses niyama but is unattached to the yamas falls; but one who possesses yama, though slack in niyama, does not sink down.

children.text: iti yamaniyamau samīkṣya buddhyā yamabahuleṣv atisaṃdadhīta buddhim ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after examining yama and niyama with intelligence, one should fix one's understanding on those in which yama predominates.
Therefore there is no consequence of falling.
Hence the well-known yamas are those beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s>.

children.text: āha kiṃ prasiddhā iti kṛtvā gṛhyante āhosvic chakyam eteṣāṃ yamānāṃ sarvajñoktaśāstrataḥ sadbhāvo vaktum ||
children.translated_text: Someone says: Are they accepted because they are well known, or can the existence of these yamas be stated from the scripture spoken by the omniscient one?

children.text: ucyate yady anyatra prasiddhā iti kva ||
children.translated_text: The answer is: if they are well known elsewhere, where is that?
That is considered there.
Why?
Because instruction has been given.
For it was said there in the sūtra, 'made from the sūtra.'

children.text: kṛtāpratiṣedhā kṛtsnā hiṃsā tantre pratiṣiddhā draṣṭavyetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that all violence not expressly permitted as done should be regarded as prohibited in the tantra.
And that violence is threefold.
It is the production of pain, the breaking of eggs, and the taking of life.

children.text: tatra duḥkhotpādanaṃ nāma krośanatarjanatāḍananirbhartsanādibahubhedo'pi caturvidhasyāpi bhūtagrāmasya manovākkāyakarmabhir abhidroho na kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, 'production of pain' means that hostility toward the fourfold host of beings, by acts of mind, speech, and body, is not to be done, even though it has many varieties such as shouting, threatening, striking, and abusing.
In this way there is <s>ahiṃsā</s> toward these living beings.

children.text: aṇḍabhedo nāma dāhatāpadhūmoparodhaparihārārtham agnikaraṇādānasampradānapratinidhānasaṃdhukṣaṇādīni na kuryāt naiva kārayet ||
children.translated_text: 'Breaking of eggs' means that, for the sake of avoiding burning, heat, smoke, and obstruction, one should not perform, nor cause another to perform, the making, taking, handing over, placing, kindling, and similar acts connected with fire.

children.text: tathā prāṇanirmocanaṃ nāma vastraśikyabhasmādhārabhaikṣyabhājanādīni muhurmuhur vivecayitavyāni ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'taking of life' means that cloth, carrying-slings, ash-containers, alms-bowls, and the like must be examined again and again.
Why?

children.text: prāṇino hi sūkṣmacāriṇaḥ kṣipram eva vilayaṃ prayānti ||
children.translated_text: For living beings that move subtly very quickly come to destruction.

children.text: tasmāt sūkṣmair aṅgapavitraiḥ pakṣmacāmaratālavṛntair vastrāntarair vā muhurmuhur vigranthodakena vā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, with fine limb-purifiers, with whisks of eyelashes, yak-tail fans, palm-leaf fans, cloth edges, or else repeatedly with water free from knots,

children.text: hariteṣu tṛṇeṣu na saṃsikte bhūpradeśe bhavati ||
children.translated_text: it should not be on green grass or on a sprinkled piece of ground.
For eight months, those of spring, summer, and winter, a mendicant should wander about.
For the sake of compassion toward all beings, he should stay in one place during the rains.

children.text: varṣābhedaṃ tu yaḥ kuryād brāhmaṇo yogadīkṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: But a Brāhmaṇa consecrated in yoga who should make a break in the rainy-season residence
is released from that sin by the <s>prājāpatya kṛcchra</s> penance.

children.text: śārīraṃ dṛśyate yatra bhayaṃ kasyāṃcid āpadi
children.translated_text: When bodily danger is seen in some calamity,
or in bad weather or the collapse of the kingdom, he may travel even during the rains.

children.text: nāsūryaṃ ca vrajenmārgaṃ nādṛṣṭāṃ bhūmim ākramet
children.translated_text: He should not travel on a road without sunlight, and he should not step on ground he has not seen.
He should always make use of thoroughly filtered water.
Whatever sin a fisherman incurs in a year,
one who collects unpurified water obtains that in a single day.

children.text: dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: He should place his foot purified by sight; he should drink water purified by cloth.
He should speak speech purified by truth, and he should act with a mind purified by reflection.
Those who are violent turn back, even if they have reached the state of <s>Brahman</s>.
Therefore one who knows yoga should not use unpurified water.

children.text: atha naṣṭe pavitre ca gṛhṇīyāt triṣu vai sakṛt
children.translated_text: Now, when the purifier has been lost, one may take it once from three sources:
from a river, from a spring, and from virtuous householders.
Stalks that are taken, and sprouting bulbs,
as well as ripe seeds: all these he should avoid.

children.text: yadā na kuryād drohaṃ ca sarvabhūteṣu dāruṇam
children.translated_text: When he commits no harsh injury toward all beings

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: by deed, mind, and speech, then he attains <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yo na hiṃsati bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
children.translated_text: He who does not injure beings, whether stationary or moving,
regarding all of them as himself, is fit for immortality.

children.text: na yajñadānairna tapo'gnihotrairna brahmacaryair na ca satyavākyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Not by sacrifices or gifts, not by austerities or fire-offerings, not by celibacies or truthful words,

children.text: na vedavidyādhyayanair vratairvā prāpyaṃ phalaṃ yady ahiṃsakasya ||
children.translated_text: nor by study of Vedic knowledge or by vows, is the fruit obtainable that belongs to the non-injuring person.

children.text: yo dadyāt kāñcanaṃ meruṃ kṛtsnāṃ caiva vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: If someone were to give gold equal to <s>Meru</s>, or the whole earth,

children.text: samudraṃ ratnapūrṇaṃ vā na tulyaṃ syādahiṃsayā ||
children.translated_text: or an ocean filled with jewels, it would not be equal to <s>ahiṃsā</s>.
Thus in this way <s>ahiṃsā</s> is established in the tantra.
Likewise <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) too is established in the tantra.
Why?

children.text: strīpratiṣedhāt indriyajayopadeśāc ca trayodaśakasya karaṇasyānutsargo brahmacaryamityuktam ||
children.translated_text: Because women are prohibited and mastery of the senses is taught; it is said that non-release of the thirteenfold instrument is <s>brahmacarya</s>.
But especially of the tongue and the organ of generation.
Here someone says: What is the purpose of the specific mention?

children.text: trayodaśakasya karaṇasyānutsargo brahmacaryamityuktvā jihvopasthayor viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ kiṃprayojanaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: After saying that <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline) is the non-release of the thirteenfold instrument, what purpose is served by making a specific mention of the tongue and the genitals?
The answer is: because of their predominance.
For the activity of the others is rooted in them.
For the activity of the others has them as its root.
How so?

children.text: jihvendriyaviṣaye upasthendriyaviṣaye vā saktaḥ trayodaśabhiḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: One who is attached to the object of the tongue-sense or to the object of the genital-sense acts through all thirteen.
Therefore this has been stated: 'specifically, of the tongue and the genitals.'
For the fall of all embodied beings has the tongue and the genitals as its cause;

children.text: tasmād amitravat paśyej jihvopasthaṃ hi mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore a human being should regard the tongue and the genitals like an enemy.

children.text: athavā manaḥpūrvakatvāt sarvavṛttīnāṃ tannigrahāt sarvavṛttīnāṃ nigrahaḥ kṛto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or, because all activities are preceded by the mind, by restraining it the restraint of all activities has been accomplished.
For it is said:
The mind is the root of all the senses in their activity;
and in auspicious and inauspicious conditions that mind of mine is well established.
Again it is also said:
With the senses extended outward there is suffering; with the senses held in there is happiness.
Therefore one should draw the self away from the forms of the senses by the self.

children.text: indriyāṇi hi tat sarvaṃ yat svarganarakāv ubhau
children.translated_text: For the senses are all that which is both heaven and hell;
when restrained or let loose, they lead to heaven and to hell.

children.text: ato janma ato duḥkhamato mṛtyubhayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: From this comes birth, from this suffering, and from this likewise the fear of death;

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgād vai tasmād etān jayāmahe ||
children.translated_text: because of attachment to the senses, therefore we shall conquer these.
Through attachment to the senses one reaches fault, without doubt;

children.text: saṃniyamya tu tānyeva tataḥ siddhiṃ niyacchati ||
children.translated_text: but by restraining those very senses one then secures accomplishment.

children.text: rajjureṣā nibandhāya yā strīṣu ramate matiḥ
children.translated_text: This is the rope for bondage: the thought that delights in women.

children.text: chittvaināṃ kṛtino yānti naināṃ tyajati duṣkṛtī ||
children.translated_text: Having cut it, the virtuous go forth; the wrongdoer does not abandon it.
Because of women there is departure from the village; for the sake of women there is buying and selling.
Women are the root of misfortunes; a wise man should not embrace one.
Poison, fire, sword, and arrow make terror plain;

children.text: māyā rūpavatī hy eṣā yāṃ striyaṃ manyate janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet this <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) possessing form is what people consider a woman.
In a body filled with impure matter, crowded with worms and creatures, naturally foul-smelling, unclean, and impermanent,

children.text: kaḍebare mūtrapurīṣabhājane ramanti mūrkhā na ramanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a vessel of urine and feces, fools take delight; the learned do not take delight.

children.text: mādyatīti striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā surāṃ pītvā na mādyati
children.translated_text: Seeing a woman, one becomes intoxicated; after drinking liquor one is not so intoxicated.
Therefore one should avoid from afar a woman who intoxicates through sight.
With downward face, without fangs, moving between the loins,
the world has been bitten by the vulva-serpent, incurable by all śāstras.
By that hairy, ugly, foul-smelling thing with bad skin,
no more than the size of a doe's hoofprint, the whole world has been blinded.
A woman is like blazing charcoal; a man is like a pot of ghee.

children.text: ye prasaktā vilīnāste ye sthitāste divaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are attached melt away; those who stand firm go to heaven.
Just as fire, increased by fuel, shines with great radiance,
so through restraint of the senses the light of one's own self shines forth.

children.text: brahmacarye sthitaṃ dhairyaṃ brahmacarye sthitaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Steadfastness is established in <s>brahmacarya</s>; austerity is established in <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: ye sthitā brahmacaryeṇa brāhmaṇā divi te sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those Brāhmaṇas who stand firm through <s>brahmacarya</s> are established in heaven.

children.text: kṣīraṃ pibanti madhu te pibanti somaṃ pibantyamṛtena sārdham
children.translated_text: They drink milk, they drink honey, they drink soma together with nectar;

children.text: mṛtyoḥ purastādamarā bhavanti ye brāhmaṇā brahmacaryaṃ caranti ||
children.translated_text: before death they become immortal, those Brāhmaṇas who practice <s>brahmacarya</s>.
Thus <s>brahmacarya</s> is established in the tantra.
Likewise <s>satya</s> (truth) is established in the tantra.
And that is twofold.
Namely: speech whose object is directly observed and real, and truthfulness of speech.

children.text: tatra paridṛṣṭārthabhūtārthaṃ vacanaṃ satyaṃ tantre siddham ||
children.translated_text: Among these, speech whose object is directly observed and real is established as truth in the tantra.
Why?
Because of the instruction of explanation and because of the instruction of the learned.
Likewise truthfulness of speech too is established in the tantra.
Why?
Because of the instruction concerning purification of speech.
Here, when one speaks what is stated in one's own śāstra, even what is false becomes truth.
Why?
Because it produces purification and increase.
For he says:
One goes to heaven by a falsehood spoken out of compassion for all beings;
but one does not go there even by truth spoken for the destruction of good people.
Again he says:

children.text: gobrāhmaṇārthe 'vacanaṃ himasti na strīṣu rājan na vivāhakāle
children.translated_text: A false statement for the sake of cows and Brāhmaṇas does not harm; not among women, O king, nor at the time of marriage;
when life is at risk or all wealth is being seized, five falsehoods are said to be non-sins.

children.text: satyaṃ brūyāt priyaṃ brūyān na brūyāt satyamapriyam
children.translated_text: One should speak truth; one should speak what is pleasant; one should not speak unpleasant truth.

children.text: priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one speak a pleasant falsehood: this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yathā hi teṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ hitamanṛtamapi satyamāpadyate evamihāpyasmākaṃ svaśāstroktaṃ bhāṣatāmanṛtamapi satyamāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: Just as, for the welfare of those very beings, even a falsehood becomes truth, so here too, when we speak what is stated in our own śāstra, even a falsehood becomes truth.
Why?
Because it has been prescribed by rule.
This too is established there.
Likewise <s>asaṃvyavahāra</s> (non-involvement in dealings) is established in the tantra.
Why?
Because of the instruction concerning the inarticulate, the dead, the mad, and the deluded.

children.text: neha loke avyaktapretonmattamūḍhāḥ saṃvyavahāraṃ kurvanti yasmād ato'trāsaṃvyavahārastantre siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this world the inarticulate, the dead, the mad, and the deluded do not conduct dealings; therefore here non-involvement in dealings is established in the tantra.
Dealings, moreover, are twofold.
Namely: dealings of buying and selling, and dealings in the royal court.
Therefore, for one engaged here in even one of these, affliction of oneself and affliction of another are unavoidable.

children.text: tatra yadyātmānaṃ pīḍayati tenehaiva loke duḥkhī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this matter, if he afflicts himself, then in this very world he becomes miserable.

children.text: syāt paraṃ pīḍayati tatrāpyasyādharmo duḥkhādiphalaḥ pracīyate ||
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, he afflicts another, then in that case too <s>adharma</s>, whose fruit is suffering and the like, accumulates for him.
By that, in the other world he experiences intense suffering.
Therefore, in both respects, such dealings are to be avoided.
For there is also the following:

children.text: yaśca pāpaṃ prakurute yaśca pāpaṃ praśaṃsati
children.translated_text: Both the one who commits sin and the one who praises sin,
the accomplice and the beneficiary: all these are equal in action.
For it has been said:

children.text: vikraye tu mahān doṣo vikrayāt patate yataḥ
children.translated_text: In selling there is great fault, since one falls through selling;

children.text: eṣa eva kraye doṣas tasmāt taṃ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: this very fault is also in buying. Therefore one should avoid it.

children.text: pracchannaṃ kurute pāpaṃ na me jānāti kaścana
children.translated_text: He commits sin secretly, thinking, 'No one knows me.'

children.text: mucyate janavādebhyas tasmāt pāpān na mucyate ||
children.translated_text: He is released from people's talk, but he is not released from sin.
Again it has been said:

children.text: ādityacandrāv anilo'nalaśca dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaśca
children.translated_text: The sun and moon, wind and fire, heaven, earth, waters, the heart, and <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: ahaśca rātriśca ubhe ca saṃdhye dharmo hi jānāti narasya vṛttam ||
children.translated_text: day and night, and both twilights: <s>dharma</s> indeed knows a man's conduct.

children.text: nārambhaśīlo na ca dambhaśīlaḥ śāstropadiṣṭāni karotyadīnaḥ
children.translated_text: Not given to undertaking works and not given to hypocrisy, undepressed, he performs what is taught by scripture;

children.text: yameṣu yukto niyameṣu caiva munir bhavaty eṣv ajaro 'maraśca ||
children.translated_text: joined to the <s>yamas</s> and likewise to the <s>niyamas</s>, the sage becomes, among these, free from old age and death.
Thus <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is established in the tantra.
Why?
Because non-possession is taught, and because there is a prohibition against food that has not been relinquished.

children.text: iha vidyamānasyāpyekasya vāsaso malavad avasthitasyāvāsopadeśāt parigrahaparityāga upadiśyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, even when there is a single garment, if it remains stained, the giving up of possessions is taught through the instruction of being without dwelling or clothing.
And what else?
Because the use of food, drink, and the like that have been abandoned is observed.
Therefore <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is established here in the tantra.
Theft, moreover, is of six kinds.

children.text: tatra adattādānam anatisṛṣṭagrahaṇam anabhimatagrahaṇam anadhikārapratigrahaḥ anupālambhaḥ aniveditopayogaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Among these are taking what has not been given, taking what has not been released, taking what is not desired, accepting what one is not entitled to accept, non-reproachful appropriation, and use without notice.
Taking what has not been given is the taking of something not given.
Taking what has not been released means carrying off the property of children, madmen, the negligent, the old, or the weak.
Taking what is not desired means carrying off goods not intended for one, such as insects, bees, birds, and moths.

children.text: anadhikārapratigraho nāma iha śāstre anabhyanujñātānām arthānāṃ gobhūhiraṇyadvipadacatuṣpadādīnāṃ grahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Accepting what one is not entitled to accept means taking things not authorized here in the scripture, such as cattle, land, gold, bipeds, quadrupeds, and the like.

children.text: anupālambho nāma kuhakakalkanaḍambhavismāpanavardhāpanādibhir upāyaiḥ parebhyo hiraṇyāc chādanopayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Non-reproachful appropriation means the use of gold or clothing from others by means such as trickery, deceitful calculation, fraud, astonishing displays, or flattery.

children.text: aniveditopayogo nāma bhakṣyabhojyalehyapeyacoṣyādīnām anyatamaṃ yatkiṃcid gurave 'niveditam upayuṅkte sa ucyate aniveditopayoga iti ||
children.translated_text: Use without notice means that if someone uses any one thing among chewable foods, cooked foods, lickables, drinks, suckables, and the like without having informed the teacher, that is called use without notice.
Thus theft is of six kinds.
The teachers call the avoidance of this theft in all its six forms <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing).
For there is also the following:

children.text: yadetad dhanamityāhuḥ prāṇā hy ete bahiścarāḥ
children.translated_text: What people call wealth is truly one's life-breaths moving outside the body;

children.text: sa tasya harate prāṇān yo yasya harate dhanam ||
children.translated_text: whoever takes another's wealth takes that person's life-breaths.
For it has been said:
The one who robs a person of everything and the one who brings life to an end:

children.text: dvāv etau samakarmāṇau tasmāt steyaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: these two have the same action. Therefore one should avoid theft.

children.text: na stenasya paro loko nāyaṃ loko durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For a thief there is no other world, nor is this world for the evil-minded man;

children.text: śaṅkitaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ drohātmā pāpa eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: suspected by all beings, he is hostile in nature and nothing but sinful.
Earth, water, likewise a vehicle, a leaf, a flower, and fruits too,
if they are not enclosed, one may take them here, when one seeks purity and has a task to perform.

children.text: nadyaśca vāpyaḥ kūpāśca taṭākāni sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Rivers, reservoirs, wells, ponds, and lakes too,
if they are not enclosed, one may take them by the rite of <s>Prājāpatya</s>.
Thus in this way <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is established in the tantra.
<s>Akrodha</s> (non-anger) is established in the tantra.
Why?
Because of the prohibition concerning <s>Śūdras</s>, and because excessive suffering is taught.

children.text: ihādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikānāṃ sarvadvaṃdvānāṃ manasi śarīre ca upanipatitānāṃ sahiṣṇutvam apratīkāraśceti yasmāt kṛto 'trākrodhas tantre siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, because endurance and non-retaliation are prescribed toward all pairs of opposites, whether internal, material, or divine, when they have fallen upon the mind and body, <s>akrodha</s> (non-anger) is established in this tantra.
Anger, moreover, is of four kinds.
They are as follows: characterized by mental disposition, characterized by action, causing bodily impairment, and causing alarm.

children.text: tatra bhāvalakṣaṇo nāma saḥ yatrāsūyādveṣamadamānamātsaryādayo bhāvāḥ pravartante ||
children.translated_text: Among these, that which is characterized by mental disposition is where states such as envy, hatred, intoxication, pride, and jealousy arise.

children.text: karmalakṣaṇo nāma yatra kalahavairasaṃpraharaṇādyā bhāvāḥ pravartante ||
children.translated_text: That which is characterized by action is where states such as quarrel, hostility, and striking arise.

children.text: vaikalyakaro nāma yatra pāṇipādanāsākṣyaṅgulipraharaṇādayo bhāvāḥ pravartante ||
children.translated_text: That which causes bodily impairment is where states such as striking the hands, feet, nose, eyes, or fingers arise.

children.text: udvegakaro nāma yatra svātmānaṃ parātmānaṃ vā prāṇair viyojayati ||
children.translated_text: That which causes alarm is where one separates oneself or another from life.
Thus anger is of four kinds.
The teachers call the avoidance of this anger in all its four forms <s>akrodha</s> (non-anger).

children.text: tasmād deśajātikulakarmasambandhanindāyāṃ karaṇakriyāyāṃ kāryanindāyām āhāranindāyāṃ vādhikṛtena krodho na kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when censure arises concerning country, birth, family, action, connection, an instrument or performance, the task itself, or food, the person concerned must not become angry.
Among these, censure of country occurs first.

children.text: tadyathā yatra bhavān jātastatra deśe brāhmaṇā eva na santīti yadi kaścidadhikṣepaṃ kuryāt tatra krodho na kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For example, if someone should make the reproach, 'In the country where you were born there are no Brāhmaṇas at all,' anger should not be shown there.
Here someone might think: 'When this is said, intense mental pain becomes manifest.
How, in this case, will anger not arise?'
The answer is: it will not arise.
Why?
Because of the power of reflective enumeration.

children.text: iha manuṣyaloke deśo'yaṃ nāma mātāpitṛhetukaḥ aupacayikaḥ kāryapiṇḍaḥ śarīrākhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here in the human world, this so-called place is the body, a mass of effects, produced from mother and father and built up by accumulation.
One's coming-to-be is from that.
But the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) is conscious, all-pervading, and pure.
And the difference between this and our position is not known.
You might say this about a matter whose object has not been directly perceived.

children.text: ataḥ krodhanimittāsaṃbhavāt parisaṃkhyānasāmarthyena krodho na kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since a cause for anger is impossible, anger is not to be produced, by the force of the enumeration.
The same should be understood also in the remaining cases.
For there is also this:
Horned, clawed, fanged, deformed, and feeding on blood,

children.text: rākṣaso vā piśāco vā krodhiṣṇur jāyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man who is prone to anger is born as a <s>rākṣasa</s> or a <s>piśāca</s>.
And again he says:
Among herons, vultures, jackals, biting insects, and mosquitoes,
and among serpents, men devoted to anger are born.
Hated by all beings, having many enemies and few kinsmen,
cruel in nature and badly behaved, a man who is prone to anger is born.

children.text: kruddhaḥ karoti pāpāni kruddhaḥ pāpāni bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Angry, he commits sins; angry, he speaks sinful words.
Angry, he becomes shameless; therefore one should completely avoid anger.
And likewise it has been said:

children.text: yat krodhano japati yac ca juhoti yadvā yadvā tapastapyati yad dadāti tatsarvam
children.translated_text: Whatever an angry man recites, whatever he offers in the fire, whatever austerity he practices, and whatever he gives, all that

children.text: vaivasvato harati pūrtamamuṣya sarvaṃ mithyā śrutaṃ bhavati tasya śamo'pi tasya ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaivasvata</s> takes away; all his meritorious work is lost, his learning becomes false, and so too his tranquility.
Blessed are those tiger-like men, those great souls, who with discernment calm anger when it has arisen,
as one calms a blazing fire with water.

children.text: yato rūpaṃ tato jñānaṃ yato jñānaṃ tatastapaḥ
children.translated_text: From form comes knowledge; from knowledge comes austerity.
From austerity comes accomplishment; from accomplishment comes forbearance.

children.text: kṣamā sarvaparaṃ mitraṃ krodhaḥ sarvaparo ripuḥ
children.translated_text: Forbearance is the highest friend of all; anger is the highest enemy of all.
This world belongs to those who possess forbearance, and the other world belongs to those who possess forbearance.

children.text: etasmāt kāraṇāt kṣantavyam ity evamakrodhastantre siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this reason one must be forbearing; in this way non-anger is established in the <s>tantra</s>.
Likewise, service to the guru is established in the <s>tantra</s>.
Why?
Because of the instruction of the commentary and the instruction of the learned.
And here it has been said, 'We shall explain the prescribed rule.'
Here the particle 'aṇ' has the sense of a limit.
The particle 'ma' has the sense of a promise.
It means, 'It exists in me.'
It means, 'It stands in me.'

children.text: yadi ceṣṭe vatsyasi yadi ceṣṭe sthāsyasi tataste vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If you wish, you will dwell; if you wish, you will remain. Then we shall tell you.
There the word 'desired' refers to the eight-limbed <s>brahmacarya</s> as the rule.

children.text: tadyathā utthānapratyutthānābhivādanagurukāryahitakārī anuttarottaravādī pūrvotthāyī jaghanyasaṃveśī preṣitāpreṣitasarvakāryakṛtajñaḥ sarvaniveditātmā dakṣo dākṣiṇyānuraktaḥ snānodvartanasaṃvāhanādibhiḥ kriyāviśeṣaiḥ chāyevānugato nityam idaṃ kṛtam idaṃ kariṣye kiṃ karavāṇīti bhūtvā gurave 'harahar vartitavyam ||
children.translated_text: It is as follows: day after day one should behave toward the guru by rising when he rises and rising to greet him, by saluting him, by doing what serves the guru's business and welfare, by not giving superior replies in return, by getting up first and lying down last, by being grateful for all tasks whether commanded or not commanded, by having the whole self submitted, by being capable, by being devoted to courtesy, by following him like a shadow with particular services such as bathing, rubbing, and massaging, and by thinking, 'This has been done; this I shall do; what shall I do?'

children.text: yastu vidyāṃ guroradhikṛtya bahubhyaḥ samprayacchati anenāsya vidyāyā dānena guravaḥ śuśrūṣitā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: But one who, after acquiring knowledge from the guru, imparts it to many people, by this gift of knowledge has served the gurus.

children.text: kṣīṇe ca brahmacarye niyataṃ guruṣu yad gauravaṃ tad brahmacaryam ||
children.translated_text: And when <s>brahmacarya</s> has ended, whatever reverence remains toward the gurus is that <s>brahmacarya</s>.
For there is also this:

children.text: gururdevo guruḥ svāmī gururmātā guruḥ pitā
children.translated_text: The guru is a god, the guru is a master, the guru is a mother, the guru is a father.

children.text: yasyaivaṃ niścito bhāvaḥ śreyastasya na dūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one whose conviction is thus settled, the highest good is not far away.
A visible object is illuminated by fire, the sun, the moon, and the stars;

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca guruvākyaiḥ prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: what has been, what is to be, and what will be are illuminated by the words of the guru.
By guides a road is traveled; by guides the ocean is crossed.
By guides heaven is reached; the guru is the guide to <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: amṛtasya pradātāraṃ yo guruṃ hy avamanyate
children.translated_text: He who disrespects the guru, the giver of immortality,
dwells in hell for sixty thousand years.
Where there is slander of the guru, where blame is being spoken,

children.text: karṇau tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato'nyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: there one should cover the ears, or go away from that place.

children.text: ācāryaṃ pūjayed yastu sarvāvasthaṃ hi nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever worships the teacher at all times and in every condition

children.text: pūjitastena bhavati śivo vai nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thereby worships <s>Śiva</s> himself; there is no doubt about this.
Taking on the form of the teacher, <s>Śiva</s> bestows knowledge.

children.text: tasmād vai nāvamantavya ācāryaḥ śreya icchatā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the teacher is not to be despised by one who desires the highest good.
For one who knows the meaning of the text and constantly points out the path of yoga,
satisfaction must be brought about by every means by one who understands.

children.text: ṛcaṃ vā yadi vārdharcaṃ pādaṃ vā yadi vākṣaram
children.translated_text: Whether it is a verse, half a verse, a quarter, or a syllable

children.text: sakāśād yasya gṛhṇīyān niyataṃ tatra gauravam ||
children.translated_text: that one receives from someone, reverence is certainly due there.

children.text: liṅgakartrī yathā mātā śāstrakartā yathā pitā
children.translated_text: As the mother is the maker of the body, and as the father is the maker of instruction,
the guru is the maker of awakening; of these, he is that great abode.
Thus, in this way, service to the guru is established in the <s>tantra</s>.
Likewise, purity is established in the <s>tantra</s>.
Why?
Because of the instruction on bathing with ash.
And that purity is threefold.

children.text: tad yathā gātraśaucaṃ bhāvaśaucam ātmaśaucaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: It is as follows: purity of the limbs, purity of disposition, and purity of the self.
There, because of the instruction on bathing with ash, purity of the limbs by means of ash is established.

children.text: āha yaduktaṃ prasiddhaṃ bhasmanā gātraśaucamiti etadevāyuktam ||
children.translated_text: He says: What was stated, 'purity of the limbs by means of ash is established,' precisely this is improper.
Why?
Because of contradiction between what precedes and what follows.

children.text: iha purastāduktaṃ prasiddhā yamā ahiṃsādayo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Here, earlier, it was said that the established restraints are non-injury and the rest.
If here again an unestablished purity of the limbs by means of ash is stated,
then this preceding and following teaching does not fit together.
And it is contradictory.
This is the fault; therefore it is due to contradiction between what precedes and what follows.
There, what was stated, 'purity of the limbs by means of ash is established,' is improper.
The reply is: this is not a fault.
Why?
Because established usage is observed.
Here too, elsewhere, bodily purification by ash is well known.
For thus it says:

children.text: saṃsargajāśca ye doṣā ye cānye pitṛmātṛjāḥ
children.translated_text: Those faults that are born from contact, and those others born from father and mother,
and the impurities produced by food and drink, mixtures that have lodged in the body,
ash burns all those, even those that have entered the bone and marrow.
And again it says:
Foods that are mixed with hair and insects, and whatever foods are spoiled,
the wise say become fit to eat as soon as they have merely been touched with ash.
Again it has also been said:

children.text: madyaṃ pītvā gurudārāṃśca gatvā steyaṃ kṛtvā brahmahatyāṃ ca kṛtvā
children.translated_text: After drinking liquor, approaching the teacher's wife, committing theft, and committing the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: bhasmoddhvasto bhasmarāśau śayāno rudrādhyāyī mucyate pātakebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who is covered with ash, lies on a heap of ash, and recites the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s> is freed from sins.

children.text: yaḥ snānam ācaren nityam āgneyaṃ saṃyatendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: The self-controlled man who daily performs the fiery bath
goes to the supreme goal, having raised up twenty-one members of his family.
Thus elsewhere too, bodily purity by ash is well known.

children.text: tasmād yuktaṃ vaktuṃ prasiddhā yamā ahiṃsādaya iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is proper to say that the <s>yamas</s>, beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-injury), are well known.
Likewise, purity of disposition is established in the tantra, since by ritual sipping, breath-control, and recitation the mind becomes unstained.
Bathing does not remove a corrupt inner disposition.
Purity of disposition is the highest purity; the rest is adornment and cleansing.
By thousands of clods of earth and by hundreds of jars of water,
evil-minded people whose thoughts are struck by sin are not purified.
Truth is purity; austerity is purity; restraint of the senses is purity;

children.text: sarvabhūtadayā śaucam adbhiḥ śaucaṃ tu pañcamam ||
