children.translated_text: compassion for all beings is purity, and purity by water is only the fifth.

children.text: śaucameva paraṃ teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ notpadyate spṛhā
children.translated_text: Purity alone is supreme for those in whom no desire arises
in receiving gifts, in undertakings, or in the objects of the senses.
Because it says:
Even if one were to give away all one's wealth with an inward self that is stained,

children.text: na tena dharmabhāg bhavati bhāva evātra kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: one does not thereby become a sharer in <s>dharma</s> (merit); the disposition alone is the cause here.

children.text: yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇīṃ kurute matim
children.translated_text: For in whatever way a person forms a wholesome intention,

children.text: tathā tathāsya sidhyanti sarvārthā nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in just that way all his aims succeed; there is no doubt about this.
Thus in this way purity of disposition is established in the tantra.
Likewise, purity of the self is established in the tantra.
Why?

children.text: yasmād avamānaparibhavaparivādādyair apahatapāpmā bhavati ityātmaśaucaṃ tantre siddham ||
children.translated_text: Because through contempt, humiliation, slander, and the like, one becomes one whose sin has been removed; thus purity of the self is established in the tantra.
For this has also been said by others:
For one who wanders over the whole earth, with its mountains, forests, and groves,
there is no discipline higher than insult, <s>Manu</s> said.
Thus in this way purity is established in the tantra.
Likewise, lightness of diet is established in the tantra.
Why?
Because of the instruction about alms-food that is left aside and obtained as it comes.

children.text: svalpamapi anupāyato'rjitamalaghu prabhūtamapi upāyato'rjitaṃ laghveva draṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: Even a little obtained by improper means should be regarded as heavy; even much obtained by proper means should be regarded as light.
For it has been said:
One should practice the bee-like way of life, comparable to the gathered mass of an anthill,
neither angry nor delighted; for that is the ancient austerity.
One who, as a matter of proper conduct, practices begging among all permissible foods
should eat and accept from approved people in their proper occupations.
One should go for alms among the four social classes, but avoid the fallen.

children.text: payaścāpaśca bhaikṣyaṃ ca samametan na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Milk, water, and alms-food are equal; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: bhaikṣyaśeṣaṃ tu yo bhikṣuryadi kiṃcit samutsṛjet
children.translated_text: If a mendicant should discard even a little remnant of alms-food,
three breath-controls, three at each morsel, must be performed.
The knower of yoga should make no store, whatever his condition may be.
Through the faults produced by storing, the ascetic becomes a worm.
Bee-like, unplanned, already set in motion, unasked-for,
and suited to each particular time: alms-food is remembered as fivefold.

children.text: gṛhād gṛhaṃ paryaṭaṃstu na gṛhaṃ parivarjayet
children.translated_text: Wandering from house to house, he should not pass over a house.
After hearing another person's statement, he should avoid a corrupt dwelling.
If a beggar passes over a good person who is uncorrupted and not fallen,

children.text: sa tasya sukṛtaṃ dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: he gives his own merit to that person and receives that person's demerit.

children.text: tathaiva ca gṛhasthasya nirāśo bhikṣuko vrajet
children.translated_text: In the same way, the beggar should go to a householder without expectation.

children.text: sa tasyeṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ca bhikṣurādāya gacchati ||
children.translated_text: The beggar goes away taking that householder's sacrificial and charitable merit.
When the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> has not been performed and a beggar has come to the house,
one should set aside the portion for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and then send the beggar away.
A beggar is able to remove faults committed in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
But the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> does not remove faults committed in connection with begging.

children.text: daśāhaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā yatra bhikṣā na labhyate
children.translated_text: Where alms are not obtained for ten days or twelve days,
the beggar should avoid that house, as a farmer avoids barren lands.
He should announce his request for alms with a four-syllabled formula.
This is the <s>dharma</s> (rule) of renouncers; the rest is buying and selling.

children.text: na hasen na cābhiprekṣet bhikṣāmicchaṃstu bhikṣukaḥ
children.translated_text: A beggar seeking alms should not laugh and should not stare.
He should stand only for the time needed to milk a cow; he should never remain waiting.
For one frightened by old age, death, wombs, and even hell,

children.text: bhayāt kṣapayate yasmāt tasmād bhaikṣyamiti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: because it wears away fear, it is therefore remembered as <s>bhaikṣya</s> (alms-food).
Those who live on curds, those who live on milk, and others who live on barley-gruel

children.text: sarve te bhaikṣyabhakṣasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: all are not worth a sixteenth part of one who lives on alms-food.
One may drink barley-gruel with cow's urine the color of heated gold

children.text: pibed dvādaśa varṣāṇi na tad bhaikṣyasamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: for twelve years, but that would not be equal to alms-food.

children.text: māsi māsi kuśāgreṇa yaḥ pibet somamagrajaḥ
children.translated_text: If, month by month, a first-born man were to drink soma with the tip of a <s>kuśa</s> blade,

children.text: bhaikṣyaṃ cāvyavahāreṇa tulyaṃ bhavati vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: it may or may not be equal to alms-food taken without worldly dealing.

children.text: bhaikṣyamannaṃ paraṃ śreyo bhaikṣyamannaṃ paraṃ śuci
children.translated_text: Alms-food is the highest good; alms-food is the highest purity

children.text: bhaikṣyaṃ hi vratināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhaikṣyameva parā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alms-food is indeed the best for those under vows; alms-food alone is the highest goal.

children.text: yadyaj jalaṃ nirdhamaneṣv apeyaṃ nadīgataṃ tat punareva peyam
children.translated_text: Whatever water is undrinkable in drains, when it has gone into a river, that same water becomes drinkable again;
so too food and drink, obtained according to rule and passed through a vessel of the twice-born, is not defiled.

children.text: lavaṇamalavaṇaṃ vā snigdham asnehikaṃ vā saharasavirasaṃ vā śuṣkamannaṃ dravaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Whether salty or without salt, oily or without oil, with flavor or without flavor, dry food or liquid,

children.text: yadi iha niravadyaṃ bhuñjate bhaikṣyamannaṃ sa khalu bhavati bhikṣurbhikṣudharmādaluptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if he eats faultless alms-food here, he indeed becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has not fallen away from the <s>bhikṣu-dharma</s>.

children.text: tathotsṛṣṭaṃ yathālabdhaṃ ca tatraivāvasaraprāptatvāt pratitantrasiddhāntasiddhaṃ sūtrato 'rthanirdeśaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, regarding what is abandoned and what is obtained as it comes, since the occasion for them has arisen right there, we shall give from the sūtra a statement of the meaning established by the doctrinal conclusion of each tantra.
Thus, in this way, lightness in food is established in the tantra.
Likewise vigilance is established in the tantra.
Why?
Because vigilance is taught, and because recitation is taught.
Here one must always be vigilant among the restraints, with mindfulness present.
For it has been said:
Vigilance, self-control, and renunciation are remembered as the horses of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
with the reins of conduct attached to them, the self is to be placed in the chariot of the mind.
Having mounted that chariot of brahman, cutting the nooses consisting of the fears of womb, birth, old age, and death,
he stands firm, having become brahman.
Thus, in this way, vigilance is established in the tantra.
In the same way the well-known yamas, beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-harm), are established.
Someone says: Because of the fault of non-specificity, the yamas are not established as well-known.
Here, for others also, <s>ahiṃsā</s> and the rest are means for accomplishing <s>dharma</s>.
And here too, in the scripture, they are just those same things.
Therefore there is non-distinction even in their being established as means and ends.
The answer is: no.
Because that would lead too far, and because it is not invariably so.

children.text: yadi dharmasādhanāstitvamātrasādharmyād ahiṃsādīnāṃ tyāgaḥ kriyate tasmāt kāryakāraṇakṣetrajñadharmādharmasukhaduḥkhasaṃsārapadārthādayo 'pi tyājyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If <s>ahiṃsā</s> and the rest are rejected because of the mere similarity that they exist as means to <s>dharma</s>, then entities such as effect, cause, <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, pleasure, pain, and saṃsāra would also have to be rejected.
If that is not so, then it is not invariably so.
Moreover, if they are rejected, actions such as deliberate violence would absurdly become means to <s>dharma</s>.
Moreover, because injunction is included within yama and niyama through excessive giving, excessive sacrifice, excessive austerity, excessive going, non-return, and the like, it is established.
And because of the qualification by a particular niyama, there is no non-specificity.

children.text: tasmād yuktamuktaṃ prasiddhā yamā ahiṃsādaya iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore what was said is proper: the well-known yamas, beginning with <s>ahiṃsā</s>, are established.
For this reason this was said: "of <s>Mahādeva</s>, the south-facing form."
Here this section on the yamas is completed.

children.text: āha tasminn āyatane prativasataḥ kā mātrā ||
children.translated_text: Someone asks: For one residing in that sacred abode, what is the measure?
It should be stated, as in the case of householders and the rest.
The answer is: no.
Because it says:
Here "one" is a number.
"Garment" occurs in the sense of covering.

children.text: tasya vāsaḥ pañcavidham aṇḍajaṃ voḍajaṃ vālajaṃ valkalajaṃ carmajaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: His garment is fivefold: made from what comes from eggs, from sheep, from hair, from bark, or from hide.

children.text: yat kuśalenābhyupāyenopapadyate tad ekapaṭalam anekapaṭalaṃ vā grāmyādibhyo niṣparigrahaṃ kaupīnapracchādanamātraṃ lajjāpratīkārārthaṃ caikaṃ vāso grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is obtained by a skillful means, whether single-layered or many-layered, free from possession in relation to village goods and the like, a single garment, merely a covering for the loin-cloth and for remedying shame, is to be accepted.

children.text: asyaiva ca sūtrasya sāmarthyāt sarvadravyaparityāge kṛte ekavāsomātraparigrahaḥ saṃskartavyaḥ śiṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: And by the force of this very sūtra, when all property has been renounced, the disciple is to be consecrated with possession of only a single garment.
Someone asks: When does his shame cease?
The answer is: through knowledge and freedom from impurity.

children.text: atra yadā prāptajñānaḥ kṣīṇakaluṣaś ca bhavati tadā tasya lajjānivṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, when he has attained knowledge and his impurity has been exhausted, then his shame ceases.

children.text: āha kiṃ vinivṛttāyām api lajjāyāṃ niyatam evaikaṃ vāso grāhyam āhosvid aniyatam iti
children.translated_text: Someone asks: Even when shame has ceased, must one definite garment still be accepted, or is it not definite?
The answer is: it is not definite, because it says:
Here the prefix a- is used in the negation of clothing.

children.text: avāsasā nagnena yathā jātena niṣparigraheṇa bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: One should be without clothing, naked, as one was born, free from possession.
Someone asks: What purpose is there in being without clothing?
That should be stated, as in the case of having one garment.

children.text: tad ucyate niṣparigrahārtham amaṅgalakhyāpanārthaṃ ceti prayojanadvayaṃ draṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: The answer is: two purposes should be understood: for the sake of non-possession, and for making known an inauspicious state.
The word "or" concerns consideration of ability and inability.
If he is unable, then he should not be naked, but should have a single garment.

children.text: yadi śaktas tadā avāsasā nagnena yathājātena niṣparigraheṇa bhavitavyam ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: If he is able, then the meaning is that he should be without clothing, naked, as he was born, free from possession.
But the word "or" is not used for optional choice.
The meaning is that such an optional sense is impossible.

children.text: āha tasminn āyatane prativasatā kim ā dehapātād anirgacchataiva stheyaṃ dhyānaikaniṣṭhena śilāvad āhosvid dṛṣṭo 'syāyatanān nirgamaḥ bhasmabhaikṣyodakārjanādinimittaṃ grāmādipraveśo vā
children.translated_text: Someone asks: While residing in that sacred abode, must he remain there without going out until the fall of the body, devoted only to meditation like a stone, or is departure from that abode observed for the sake of obtaining ash, alms-food, water, and the like, or entrance into a village and so on?
The answer is: it is observed.
Because:

children.text: atra mūtraṃ ca purīṣaṃ ca mūtrapurīṣam
children.translated_text: Here urine and excrement together are "urine-excrement".

children.text: cārthe dvaṃdvasamāsaḥ atra mūtraṃ nāma yad etad udaraparyuṣitaṃ niḥsarati bahiḥ sravati tan mūtram ||
children.translated_text: The compound is a dvandva in the sense of "and". Here "urine" means that which, having remained in the belly, comes out and flows outside; that is urine.
It is called urine because of release.
For the meaning is that urine is well known in common usage and the like through its relation to urinenness.

children.text: purīṣaṃ nāma yad etat pītakhāditāvalīḍhānām āhāraviśeṣāṇām ādhyātmikena agninā paripakvam apānena skhalati tat purīṣam ||
children.translated_text: Excrement means that which, among particular foods that have been drunk, eaten, and licked, is cooked by the internal fire and drops down by the apāna.

children.text: purān nirgatatvāt purīṣatvābhisambandhād vā purīṣaṃ lokādiprasiddham ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that it is excrement, well known in common usage, because it has come out from the body, or because of its relation to excrement-ness.
The letter na is a prohibition of seeing.
The meaning is: it should not be seen.

children.text: ava iti apavarjanaṃ nāma pratiṣedhe jātigrahaṇendriyāntarapratiṣedhe cety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Ava" means avoidance; it has the sense of prohibition, of taking a class, and of prohibiting the other senses.
The root <s>īkṣ</s> is in the sense of seeing.

children.text: yad etan nijaṃ buddhīndriyaṃ cakṣur anena cakṣuṣā anayā buddhyā manuṣyādīnāṃ mūtrapurīṣaṃ na draṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: This eye is one's own cognitive organ; with this eye, with this faculty of understanding, the urine and feces of humans and the like should not be looked at.
But not those of cows and the like: that is the meaning.
Someone asks: Is only the mere sight of urine and feces prohibited for him?
The answer is: no.
For he says:

children.text: atra strī ca śūdraś ca strīśūdram ||
children.translated_text: Here, woman and <s>Śūdra</s> together are meant by the expression <s>strīśūdram</s>.
It is a copulative compound in the sense of 'and.'

children.text: atra strī nāma seyaṃ lokaprasiddhā stanajaghanakeśavatī hāvabhāvavilāsayuktā puruṣabhāvasvabhāvikā divyā mānuṣā atiratirasā viṣayamūrtir iti kṛtvā pratiṣidhyate ||
children.translated_text: Here 'woman' means this one who is well known in the world, possessing breasts, hips, and hair, endowed with gestures, expressions, and playful charm, naturally connected with a man's passion, whether divine or human, an embodiment of an object of sense because she has the flavor of excessive passion; on that basis she is prohibited.

children.text: anubhāṣaṇapūrvikā cāsyāḥ prāptir bhaviṣyatītyataḥ strī nābhibhāṣitavyety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since access to her would be preceded by conversation, the meaning is that a woman must not be addressed.
A <s>Śūdra</s> means this person well known from ordinary usage and the like as an attendant of the three varṇas.
He is called <s>Śūdra</s> from grieving and from injuring.

children.text: sa khalv adayālur iti kṛtvā pratiṣidhyate ||
children.translated_text: Since he is merciless, he too is prohibited.
For what reason?

children.text: tenākruṣṭaś cābhihataś ca vā kruddhas tadvadhārthaṃ pravartate ato jātijñānatapaḥśrutahānir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If one is abused or struck by him, one becomes angry and sets out to kill him; therefore there is loss of birth-status, knowledge, austerity, and learning.
And when the absence of disrespect and the like has been indicated, because disrespect and the like are absent, there is absence of <s>sūci</s> and increase.
In the <s>akaluṣa-sūtra</s> we shall make a statement of his fault.
The negative particle is used in the prohibition of speech.
The meaning is: it must not be addressed.
The word <s>abhi</s> means occasion or application.
The meaning is that, in a prohibition, when the class is mentioned, the other prohibition too is included.
The root <s>bhāṣ</s> is in the sense of articulate speech.

children.text: yad etat karmendriyaṃ vāg anayā vāṇyā iti ||
children.translated_text: This organ of action, namely speech, with this voice: thus it is explained.
Therefore the meaning is that a woman and a <s>Śūdra</s> must not be addressed.

children.text: āha nāvekṣen nābhibhāṣed ity ukte 'tha kim anena sādhakenāndhamūkavad avasthātavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Someone asks: When it has been said, 'He should not look' and 'He should not address,' must this practitioner then remain like a blind and mute man?
The answer is: no.
For he says:
Here the repeated word 'if, if' is used in the sense of an anticipated possibility.

children.text: nābhibhāṣed iti vacanān niṣiddhe 'py arthe gurvartham ātmārthaṃ vā bhasmabhaikṣyodakārjanādinimittaṃ grāmādīn praviṣṭasya viṇmūtrayoḥ strīśūdrayoś ca darśanam abhibhāṣaṇaṃ ca bhaviṣyatīti kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Although the object is prohibited by the statement 'he should not address,' when one has entered villages and the like for the sake of the teacher or for one's own sake, for the purpose of obtaining ash, alms, water, and so on, there may be seeing of excrement and urine and of women and <s>Śūdras</s>, and there may also be addressing them.

children.text: ata etad uktaṃ sarvajñena bhagavatā yady avekṣed yady abhibhāṣed iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this was said by the omniscient blessed one: 'if he should look, if he should address.'
The meaning is that it would necessarily occur.

children.text: āha dṛṣṭe cābhibhāṣite copahatena nirghātanaṃ kiṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Someone asks: When there has been seeing and addressing, what removal should be performed by one who has been impaired?
That is answered: <s>upasparśana</s>.
Because:
Here <s>upa</s> is in the sense of acceptance or approach.
The meaning is: through acceptance, by one whose mind is tainted.
<s>Spṛśya</s> means simply the joining of the substance of ash with the limbs of the body.
<s>Upaspṛśya</s> is a synonym for bathing.
It is like contact with water while clothed.
And that is to be done with ash, not with water.
Why?
Because that would contradict what precedes and what follows.
And because bathing is not relevant here.
<s>Upaspṛśya</s> is a completed-action form.

children.text: āha upaspṛśya yadi kaluṣaṃ na kṣīṇaṃ syāt tato nirghātanaṃ kiṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Someone asks: If, after touching in this way, the taint should not be destroyed, then what removal should be performed?

children.text: tad ucyate sākāṅkṣatvān niṣṭhāśabdasya prāṇāyāmaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is answered: because the completed-action word has an expectancy, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> must be performed.
For he says:

children.text: atra prāṇo nāma ya eṣa mukhanāsikābhyāṃ niḥsarati vāyur eṣa prāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>prāṇa</s> is the air that comes out through the mouth and the nose; this is <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasya āyāmo nigraho nirodhaḥ sa prāṇāyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its <s>āyāma</s>, that is, restraint, control, or obstruction, is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
And it should be understood as an activity of the person.
Why?
Because <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is preceded by knowledge, desire, and effort.
It may be with one impulse or with two impulses.
Likewise it may be of twenty measures, twenty-four measures, or thirty measures.
A measure is the time of the blinking of an eye.
It should be done according to one's capacity and according to one's strength.

children.text: tasmād upaspṛśya padmakasvastikopasthāñjalikārdhacandrapīṭhakadaṇḍāyatasarvatobhadrādīnām anyatamenāsanabandhena prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā upaviśyaitāny aṅgāni kṛtvā grīvām unnāmya pūraṇapūrvako vā recakapūrvako vā tāvat kartavyo yāvan nigṛhītā vāyavo dhyānībhūtaś ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after performing <s>upasparśana</s>, having sat facing east or north in any one bound posture such as <s>Padmaka</s>, <s>Svastika</s>, <s>Upastha</s>, <s>Añjalika</s>, <s>Ardhacandra</s>, <s>Pīṭhaka</s>, <s>Daṇḍāyata</s>, <s>Sarvatobhadra</s>, and the like, having arranged these limbs, raising the neck, and beginning either with inhalation or with exhalation, it should be performed until the breaths are restrained and he has become meditative.

children.text: tatra dhyānībhūto nāma yadā dantivad antaḥśarīraṃ pūrṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: There, 'having become meditative' means that the inner body becomes full like an elephant.

children.text: nigṛhītānāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ yadā kūrmavad antaḥśarīre ucchvāsapratyucchvāsā vartante svacchendriyaś ca bhavati tadā mantavyā nigṛhītā vāyava iti ||
children.translated_text: The mark of the restrained breaths is this: when inhalations and counter-inhalations move within the inner body like a tortoise, and when the senses are clear, then the breaths should be regarded as restrained.

children.text: tataḥ śanaiḥ śanair moktavyā nāsikayā yathotpalapattram api nāsāpuṭasthaṃ na kampayati ||
children.translated_text: Then they should be released very slowly through the nose, so that even a lotus petal placed at the nostril would not tremble.

children.text: tad atra praśnākrāntau krameṇākramitavyaḥ antarbhāve 'ntare vāyavo bhāvayitavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus here, when the question has been entered upon, one must proceed in sequence; with internalization, the breaths are to be contemplated within.
The root <s>an</s> is in the sense of breathing.
The prefix <s>āṅ</s> refers to the limit marked by binding the posture, stilling, restraint, destruction of taint, release, and so forth.
The root <s>yam</s> is in the sense of binding.
They are to be bound.
The root <s>ḍukṛñ</s> should be understood in the sense of doing.
The suffix <s>tvā</s> denotes completion of an action.
The meaning is: as with a cutting off.

children.text: āha atha kṛte prāṇāyāme yadi kaluṣaṃ na kṣīṇaṃ syāt tato 'nena kiṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Someone asks: Now, if after <s>prāṇāyāma</s> has been performed the taint should not be destroyed, then what should he do?
That is answered: recitation is to be done.
For he says:

children.text: atra tvāśabdasāmarthyād gamyate prāṇasaṃyamena samaṃ japyaṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the force of the word <s>tvā</s>, it is understood that recitation is to be done together with restraint of the breath.
as in the case of <s>upasparśana</s> (ritual touching or sipping of water).
Therefore here there is the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> mantra named <s>Raudrī</s>.
And why is it called <s>Raudrī</s>?
Because it makes <s>Rudra</s> present, it is <s>Raudrī</s>.

children.text: rudro vāsyāṃ cintyate rudraprāpakatvād vā raudrī ||
children.translated_text: Or it is <s>Raudrī</s> because <s>Rudra</s> is contemplated in it, or because it brings one to <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: āha sadyojātādibahuprakārā tatra kā sā raudrī ||
children.translated_text: One says: among the many forms beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>, which one there is <s>Raudrī</s>?
That is answered: <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Here the one that is <s>Raudrī</s> is <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
And why is it called <s>Gāyatrī</s>?
Because, being sung, it protects the singer.

children.text: gāyatre vā chandasi vartata iti gāyatrī ||
children.translated_text: Or it is <s>Gāyatrī</s> because it occurs in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre.
Here, by the mention of <s>Raudrī</s>, Vedic and other <s>Gāyatrīs</s> are excluded.
But here, by the mention of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the forms beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s> are excluded.
The word '<s>Gāyatrīm</s>' is the object of the action.
<s>Bahurūpī</s> is the one named <s>Aghorā</s>.
And why is it called <s>Bahurūpī</s>?
It is <s>Bahurūpī</s> because it occurs in the forms included among the stated forms of <s>Bahurūpa</s>.

children.text: bahurūpo vā asyāṃ cintyata iti bahurūpaprāpakatvād bahurūpī ||
children.translated_text: Or, because <s>Bahurūpa</s> is contemplated in it, it is <s>Bahurūpī</s>, since it brings one to <s>Bahurūpa</s>.
The word '<s>Bahurūpīm</s>' is the object of the action.
The word '<s>vā</s>' is used in the sense of option.

children.text: ubhayor api brahmatvam ubhayor api tulyārthasādhakatvam ubhe api maheśvaraparigṛhīte ity ata ekām anekāṃ vā upaspṛśya japed iti mānasī kriyety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since both have the status of <s>brahman</s>, both accomplish the same purpose, and both are accepted by <s>Maheśvara</s>, therefore the meaning is that, having performed <s>upasparśana</s> with one or with many, one should recite; this is a mental act.
One asks: for the person qualified for <s>upasparśana</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and recitation, what result is accomplished?
That is answered: freedom from defilement.
For this reason he says:
Thus.

children.text: atra akaluṣā yasya matiḥ so 'yam akaluṣamatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, one whose mind is untainted is this '<s>akaluṣamati</s>', a person of untainted mind.
It is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound.
Here the prefix <s>a</s>- negates defilement.
In this context defilement is precisely defilement of mental states.
How is that known?
Because it has already been established earlier.
And here it was stated before:

children.text: nāvekṣen nābhibhāṣed ity ukte arthāpannaṃ dṛṣṭe cābhibhāṣite ca dveṣecchākrodhā utpadyante ||
children.translated_text: When it is said, 'One should not look, one should not address,' it is implied that, when one has seen and addressed them, hatred, desire, and anger arise.
And when those have arisen, they become manifest in the mind.
It is like seeing a black mark or a tilaka and the like.

children.text: abhivyakteś cocyate kaluṣito 'haṃ vyāhato 'haṃ malinīkṛto 'ham iti ||
children.translated_text: And because of that manifestation one says, 'I am defiled, I am obstructed, I have been made impure.'
Therefore, because they occasion hatred, desire, and anger, the prohibition concerning urine, feces, women, and <s>Śūdras</s> is made.

children.text: yadā tv ete dveṣādayo bhāvā bījakṣaye sati notpadyante tadā paraṃ bhāvaśaucaṃ pratyavagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: But when these states such as hatred do not arise once the seed has been destroyed, then the supreme purity of one's condition should be understood.
This is the phrase 'of one whose mind is defiled.'
And defilement is occasional, dependent on a cause.

children.text: na ca nimittānityatvān naimittikaṃ nityaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Nor, because the cause is impermanent, does what depends on that cause become permanent.
It is like a sprout when the seed has been destroyed.

children.text: na ca yatraiva kaluṣam utpadyate tatraivopasparśanādīni kartavyāni ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it the case that <s>upasparśana</s> and the other rites must be performed exactly wherever defilement arises.
Rather, they are to be performed at the <s>āyatana</s> (sanctuary).

children.text: athāpi kaluṣam utpannaṃ pradhvastaṃ syāt tathāpi tadarthaṃ na kartavyāni ||
children.translated_text: And even if defilement has arisen and then ceased, they are still not to be performed for its sake.

children.text: yadā tu tad avasthitaṃ sambhavati śirorogādivat tadā kartavyāni ||
children.translated_text: But when it can remain in place, as in the case of a disease of the head and the like, then they are to be performed.

children.text: atra matir iti buddhir ity anarthāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Here '<s>mati</s>' and '<s>buddhi</s>' do not differ in meaning.
Here too, the meaning is that purity of the self is explained by designating the instrument.
One asks: what is to be done by the practitioner whose mind is untainted?
That is answered: he should practice.
For this reason he says:
Here the word 'of one practicing' authorizes the acquisition of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: bhaikṣyacaraṇavat tapaś caritavyaṃ vihartavyaṃ tapaso 'rjanaṃ kartavyaṃ na stheyam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As with going for alms, <s>tapas</s> should be practiced and carried on; the acquisition of <s>tapas</s> should be done, and one should not remain still. This is the meaning.
The phrase 'of one practicing' is in the present tense.

children.text: akaluṣamateś carato vā asya kā kāryaniṣpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, for this person of untainted mind who is practicing, what result is accomplished?
That is answered:
Here the word '<s>tataḥ</s>' refers to practice.

children.text: tataḥ caryābhiniveśād anantaraṃ tajjanyadharmād ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus it means: immediately after devotion to practice, or from the <s>dharma</s> produced by that practice.
The word '<s>asya</s>' refers to the practitioner.
That is, it refers to the one who, having an untainted mind, practices.
One asks: what happens?
That is answered: yoga begins to function.

children.text: adhyayanadhyānādilakṣaṇaḥ kriyāyogaś carataḥ pravartata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who practices, <s>kriyāyoga</s>, marked by study, meditation, and the like, begins to function. This is the meaning.
Here yoga should be understood as the connection of the self with the Lord.
The prefix '<s>pra</s>' has the sense of an initial action, a beginning.

children.text: yadā akaluṣamatiś carati tadā pravartata ity arthāt ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that when the person of untainted mind practices, then it begins to function.
There, from what does it begin to function?
From the sense-objects.
That which begins to function for one whose mind has been withdrawn from the objects is yoga.
In what manner does it begin to function?
Gradually.
By what does it begin to function?
It begins to function by means of <s>tapas</s>.
For whom does it begin to function?
For the self, the practitioner.
In what does it begin to function?

children.text: yo 'yam ātmany ātmabhāvaḥ sa maheśvare pravartata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that this state of selfhood in the self begins to function in <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: evaṃ yasmād dravyāvasthānakāladeśakriyāprayogoccāvacaprayojanayamaniyamavṛttivasatyarthaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāranimittapratiṣedhasaṃśayanirghātanaśaucaniyogaphalopāyāś ca vyākhyātāḥ ato 'trāyatanaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since substance, abiding, time, place, action, application, various purposes, <s>yama</s> and <s>niyama</s>, mode of life, dwelling, object, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s>, cause, prohibition, the removal of doubts, the injunction of purity, results, and means have been explained, the section on the <s>āyatana</s> is completed here.
Here one asks: is the <s>tantra</s> grounded in its purpose?
The answer is: no.
It is grounded in yoga.

children.text: yasmād āha yuktottare saty api padārthavailakṣaṇye raṅgapatākādivacchiṣyapralobhanārtham idam ārabhyate ||
children.translated_text: For he says: even when what is subsequent to yoga exists, and although the categories are distinct, this is begun for the sake of enticing disciples, like a stage, a banner, and the like.

children.text: atra dūraṃ nāma yad etad darśanādyaṃ vikaraṇāntaṃ māheśvaram aiśvaryam anena kadācit prāptapūrvakaṃ tasmiṃs tatprāptau ca ||
children.translated_text: Here what is called 'distant' is this <s>Māheśvara</s> sovereignty, beginning with vision and ending with <s>vikaraṇa</s>; by it, something had at some time been attained before, and it concerns that and the attainment of that.
In the cases of vision and the rest, the word 'distant' here should be understood as the governing term.
And the attainment of that comes from the arising of yoga.
One asks: if this is so, let vision and the rest be stated from the <s>sūtra</s>.
They are being stated.

children.text: darśanam ity atrāpi ca nastrikaṃ cintyate ||
children.translated_text: And here too, in the term 'vision', a triad is to be considered.
The seer, vision, and what is to be seen.
Here the seer is the <s>siddha</s> (accomplished one).
Vision is his <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), namely knowledge.
The things to be seen are forms.

children.text: tat kṛtsneṣu viṣayeṣu samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣataś ca darśanaṃ pravartata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that vision operates with regard to all objects in summary, expansion, division, and particular distinction.

children.text: tathā śravaṇam ity atrāpi nastrikaṃ cintyante ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the term 'hearing' too, a triad is to be considered.
The hearer, hearing, and what is to be heard.
There the hearer is the <s>siddha</s>.
Hearing is his <s>siddhi</s>, namely knowledge.
The things to be heard are sounds.

children.text: tad asya siddhasya śrāvyeṣv artheṣu samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣataś ca śravaṇaṃ pravartata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, for this <s>siddha</s>, hearing operates with regard to audible objects in summary, expansion, division, and particular distinction.

children.text: tathā mananam ity atrāpi ca nastrikaṃ cintyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the term 'reflection' too, a triad is to be considered.
The thinker, thinking, and what is to be thought.
Here the thinker is the <s>siddha</s>.
Thinking is his <s>siddhi</s>, namely knowledge.
The things to be thought are the minds of others.
The meaning is that he becomes the thinker of the minds concerned with <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation among gods, humans, and beings born in animal wombs.

children.text: tathā vijñānam ity atrāpi nastrikaṃ cintyante ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the term 'cognition' too, a triad is to be considered.
The knower, cognition, and what is to be cognized.
There the knower is the <s>siddha</s>.
Cognition is his <s>siddhi</s>, namely knowledge.
The things to be cognized are mental operations.

children.text: asya siddhasya pravartante svataḥ prādurbhavantīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They proceed for this <s>siddha</s>; that is, they appear of themselves.
Does he have knowledge, or not?
It is said: he does.
For he says:

children.text: atrokteṣu dṛśyaśravyādiṣu ca aśeṣeṣu siddheśvarapaśvādiṣu nirviśeṣavācī sarvaśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, with regard to the visible, audible, and other things already mentioned, and with regard to all <s>siddhas</s>, <s>īśvaras</s>, <s>paśus</s>, and the like without remainder, the word 'all' should be understood as denoting without distinction.

children.text: jñatā ity atrāpi ca nas trikaṃ cintyate ||
children.translated_text: And in the term 'knowledge' too, a triad is to be considered by us.
The knower, knowledge, and what is to be known.

children.text: tatra jñātā siddhaḥ jñānam asya siddhir jñānam ||
children.translated_text: There the knower is the <s>siddha</s>; knowledge is his <s>siddhi</s>, namely knowledge.
What is to be known is effect, cause, and the <s>siddhas</s>.
Therefore a single power of knowledge, though one, is figuratively treated in many ways because of the immeasurable and manifold knowable object.

children.text: sphaṭikādityavac cāsya sarvataḥ pravartata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the meaning is that it operates everywhere, like crystal and the sun.

children.text: āha kim ayaṃ siddho jñānamātrasaṃtuṣṭaḥ paṅguvad uta kriyāśaktir apy asti neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: is this <s>siddha</s> satisfied with mere knowledge, like a lame man, or does he also have a power of action?
It is said: he has it.
For he says:
Here, because it is acquired adventitiously, the power of complete knowledge has been stated.
The meaning is: not as in the case of being a seer or being a Brahmin.

children.text: yasmāt atra manojavavad ity evaṃ prāpte samānopamānatvān manojavitvam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: For, when the expression 'like the speed of the mind' would have been expected here, 'mind-swiftness' was stated because the comparison is the same.
Like the speed of the mind.
One asks:
What is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>?

children.text: ucyate yādṛṅ manaso javitvam āśukāritvam īdṛśam asya siddhasya kartṛtve śīghratvam ||
children.translated_text: It is said: just as the mind has speed, quick efficacy, so this <s>siddha</s> has quickness in agency.

children.text: na cāsya prajāpativat taponimittatvād bhāvottarā pravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And his activity is not, as in the case of <s>Prajāpati</s>, subsequent to an intention because its cause is <s>tapas</s>.

children.text: kiṃtu bhāvasya balīyastvāt pravṛtter utpannasvabhāvaḥ karomīti kṛtam eva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Rather, because the intention is stronger, activity has an arisen nature: when he thinks 'I am doing it,' it is already done.
Or when he thinks, 'I am destroying it,' it has been destroyed.
Why?
Because vision and action are unobstructed.

children.text: tvam iti bhāvanirdeśād gamyate vittam asya śaktiḥ sāmarthyam ||
children.translated_text: From the designation of the state as 'you,' it is understood that his possession is power, capacity.
The meaning is: such is his <s>aiśvarya</s> (lordly power).

children.text: āha kim asya siddhasya kartavyaṃ karaṇaṃ kuto vā karoti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: what is to be done by this <s>siddha</s>, what is the instrument, and from what does he act?
That is answered.

children.text: kāmarūpī ity atrāpi ca nas trikaṃ cintyate ||
children.translated_text: And in the term 'taking whatever form he desires' too, a triad is to be considered.
The desirer, desire, and what is desired.
There the desirer is the <s>siddha</s>.
Desire is his wish.
The desired things are forms.
How so?
The root kam occurs in the sense of wishing.

children.text: rūpāṇi yāvanti yādṛśāni cecchati tāvanti tādṛśāni ca karoti ||
children.translated_text: However many forms, and of whatever kind, he wishes, just so many and of just that kind he makes.
And the instruments by which he makes forms, earth and the other elements, are subject to himself.

children.text: vibhutvāc ca karaṇānāṃ yatra yatra rūpāṇy abhinirvartayati tatra tatra cāsya buddhyādīnāṃ karaṇānāṃ vṛttilābho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And because the instruments are pervasive, wherever he produces forms, there too the operation of his instruments such as intellect is obtained.
This follows from the example of the eye and the other senses.
If it is objected, 'He is not the presiding controller,'
that is not so.
Why?
Because he says 'possessing form.'
Here he is 'possessing form' because he presides over forms.
It is like one who possesses a staff.

children.text: rūpivacanāc ca sarveṣām eva rūpāṇāṃ yugapad evādhiṣṭhātā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And because of the statement 'possessing form,' he is the simultaneous presiding controller of all forms.
Because of his pervasiveness he is not different from <s>Maheśvara</s>.
And this is understood from the statement of union with <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: tvam iti bhāvanirdeśād gamyate vittam asya śaktiḥ sāmarthyam ||
children.translated_text: From the designation of the state as 'you,' it is understood that his possession is power, capacity.
The meaning is: such is his <s>aiśvarya</s>.
One asks: because incapacity is observed in limited acts, there is doubt.

children.text: atha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ svakṛtānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ saṃhāre śaktaḥ uta viśvāmitravad aśaktaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, is this <s>siddha</s> capable of withdrawing those forms made by himself, or is he incapable, like <s>Viśvāmitra</s>?
It is said:
For he says:
Here vi means destruction, separation.
He becomes <s>vikaraṇa</s> (without instruments).
It is like one without arrows or without a chariot.
Because the instrument is negated, the effect is also negated.
Why?
Because the instruments are particular, receptive, and subtle.
Therefore, as <s>vikaraṇa</s>, there is <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation).

children.text: āha aviśeṣād iha sāṃkhyayogādīnām api sahaiśvaryeṇa kāryakaraṇatyāgaṃ kṛtvā kaivalyaniṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: One asks: because there is no distinction here, do <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and the other systems too, after abandoning effect and instrument together with <s>aiśvarya</s>, have establishment in <s>kaivalya</s>?
And here too, in the <s>śāstra</s>:
How, then, on that basis is there no distinction?

children.text: atha matiḥ niratiśaye mokṣe nāsti vaiṣamyaṃ tathāpy atidānādibhiḥ sādhyasādhananiṣṭhāto 'tha viśeṣaḥ ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the thought is: in unsurpassed liberation there is no inequality, yet there is a distinction because of establishment in the means and the goal through <s>atidāna</s> and the like, this is stated:
There is no absence of distinction.
Because he says:
Here, by the property of the qualities, this person becomes a bearer of properties.

children.text: yad etad darśanādyaṃ vikaraṇāntaṃ māheśvaram aiśvaryam asyeśaprasādāt svaguṇasaṃvṛttaṃ tenāyaṃ guṇadharmeṇa dharmī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Māheśvara</s> sovereignty, beginning with vision and ending with <s>vikaraṇa</s>, belongs to him through the favor of the Lord and has arisen as his own quality; by that property of the qualities, he becomes a bearer of properties.
Why?
It is understood from the designation of the state in the word 'you'.

children.text: ṛte 'pi kāryakaraṇe jñātā kartā ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Even apart from the effect and the instrument, he is a knower and an agent.

children.text: tataś ca kaivalyādyāḥ sarvaniṣṭhā viśeṣitā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And therefore all the final states, beginning with isolation, become distinguished.
The word 'and' here is for attributing the powers of knowledge and action.

children.text: evam atrāsya siddhasya kāmarūpivikaraṇavacanāt svakṛteṣu rūpeṣu prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ guṇadharmitvaṃ ca vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because this perfected one is described here as assuming forms at will and as possessing <s>vikaraṇa</s>, his mastery, pervasion, and being a bearer of qualities in forms made by himself have been explained.

children.text: etad yuktottare prasādād guṇāḥ pravartanta ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the passage immediately following this, the meaning is that the qualities proceed because of grace.
Here this authoritative section on sovereignty is completed.

children.text: āha kiṃ parakṛteṣv api devamanuṣyatiryagyonirūpeṣv asya siddhasya prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ cāsti neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: does this perfected one also have mastery and pervasion in forms made by others, namely forms with divine, human, or animal births, or not?
The answer is: he does.
Because he says:

children.text: atra sarve niravaśeṣāḥ paśudharmāṇa ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the meaning is that all, without exception, are properties of <s>paśu</s>s.
The word 'and' serves to combine forms made by oneself and forms made by others.

children.text: parakṛteṣv api devādirūpeṣu prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ cāstīti ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that there is mastery and pervasion even in forms made by others, such as divine forms.
'Of him' means 'of the perfected one'.
'Subject to control' means 'obedient'.
And the meaning is that they become subject to his will.
'They become' is a statement of fact, without doubt.

children.text: āha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ kadācid vaśyo bhavati neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: does this perfected one ever become subject to their control, or not?
The answer is: no.
Because he says:
Here too the word 'all' applies only to <s>paśu</s>s.
'Of all' is used with inclusion of the lesser.
The word 'and' has the sense of superiority.

children.text: abhyadhika utkṛṣṭo vyatiriktaś ca bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that he is superior, excellent, and distinct.
This is the word 'not subject to control'.
The letter <s>a</s> negates a previous condition of being subject to control.
'He becomes' is a statement of fact, without doubt.

children.text: yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarveṣāṃ śakter avaśyo bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that when the perfected one, endowed with the qualities and having attained sovereignty, is present, then he is not subject to the power of all.

children.text: āha kiṃ svaśaktyādhyākrāntā vaśyā bhavanti āhosvid dharmamaryādāṃ rakṣanti guruśiṣyavat ||
children.translated_text: One asks: do they become subject to control because they are overpowered by his own power, or do they preserve the bounds of <s>dharma</s>, like teacher and pupil?
A capable pupil of a teacher is not overpowered.
Because he says:

children.text: atrāpi sarvaśabdaḥ paśuṣv eva niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here too the word 'all' should be understood as referring to <s>paśu</s>s without exception.
The word 'and' combines this with what was previously stated.

children.text: na kevalam asya te vaśyāḥ kiṃ tv āveśyāś ceti ||
children.translated_text: They are not only subject to his control; rather, they are also subject to being entered by him.
Here the prefix <s>āṅ</s> specifies the limit of entering.
The root <s>viś</s> is used in the sense of entering.

children.text: sa tasya jñānakriyayor vibhutve 'pi śaktisaṃyogād āviśya pratyayalopaṃ kartuṃ samartho bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, although that being has pervasion with respect to knowledge and action, through conjunction with power he is able to enter it and cause the disappearance of awareness.

children.text: āha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ kadācid āveśyo bhavati neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: does this perfected one ever become subject to being entered by them, or not?
The answer is: no.
Because he says:
Here too the word 'all' applies only to <s>paśu</s>s.
'Of all' is used with inclusion of the lesser.
The word 'and' has the sense of superiority.
The meaning is that he is superior, excellent, and distinct.
This is the word 'not subject to being entered'.
The letter <s>a</s> negates a previous condition of being subject to being entered.
He possesses the property of not being enterable.

children.text: na vyādhiśeṣavad avasthānam bhavati iti bhūtārthavādo niḥsaṃśayam ||
children.translated_text: 'He does not remain like the remnant of a disease' is a statement of fact, without doubt.

children.text: yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarveṣāṃ cānāveśyo bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that when the perfected one, endowed with the qualities and having attained sovereignty, is present, then he is also not enterable by all.

children.text: āha kim āveśanamātra eva śakto yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācādivad uta prāṇair api viprayogaṃ yātanābhiś ca saṃyogaṃ kartuṃ śakto bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: is he capable only of entering, like <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>rākṣasa</s>s, <s>piśāca</s>s, and the like, or is he also able to separate them from their life-breaths and join them with torments?
The answer is: he is capable.
Because he says:

children.text: atrāpi sarvaśabdaḥ paśuṣv eva niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here too the word 'all' should be understood as referring to <s>paśu</s>s without exception.
The word 'and' has the sense of combination.

children.text: na kevalam asya te vaśyāḥ āveśyāś ca kiṃtu vadhyāś ceti ||
children.translated_text: They are not only subject to his control and subject to being entered by him; rather, they are also vulnerable to being killed by him.
'Of him' is a reference to the perfected one.
This is the word 'killable'.
The root <s>vadh</s> is used in the sense of separation from the life-breaths and also in the sense of torment.

children.text: prāṇair api viprayogaṃ yātanābhiś ca saṃyogaṃ kartuṃ samartho bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that he is able to separate them even from their life-breaths and to connect them with torments.
'They become' is a statement of fact, without doubt.

children.text: yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarve cāsya vadhyā bhavantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that when the perfected one, endowed with the qualities and having attained sovereignty, is present, then all are also vulnerable to being killed by him.

children.text: āha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ kadācid vadhyo bhavati neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: does this perfected one ever become vulnerable to being killed by them, or not?
The answer is: no.
Because he says:
Here too the word 'all' applies only to <s>paśu</s>s.
'Of all' is used with inclusion of the lesser.
The word 'and' has the sense of superiority.
The meaning is that he is superior, excellent, and distinct.
This is the word 'not killable'.
The letter <s>a</s> negates a previous condition of being killable.

children.text: yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarveṣāṃ cāvadhyo bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that when the perfected one, endowed with the qualities and having attained sovereignty, is present, then he is also not killable by all.

children.text: evaṃ parakṛteṣvapi devādiśarīreṣu rūpeṣu prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ ca vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: Thus mastery and pervasion in forms made by others, namely divine and other such bodies, have also been explained.
Here this section of six sūtras is completed.

children.text: āha kim asya siddhasyaitadaiśvaryaṃ nityam āhosvit pārthivāpyataijasavāyavyavyomamānasāhaṃkārikamahadātmakādivad anityam iti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: is this lordly power of this accomplished one eternal, or is it impermanent like what consists of earth, water, fire, wind, ether, mind, ego, the great principle, and so forth?
The answer is: it is eternal.
Because he says:
Here, because it conflicts with the statement beginning 'imperishable,' the reading 'he studies and practices' is unsuitable.

children.text: tasmād atītānāgatavartamānakālabhayaṃ na vidyata ity ato 'bhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because fear connected with past, future, and present time does not exist, he is called fearless.

children.text: āha abhītānām api brahmādīnāṃ saṃhāre kṣayaḥ śrūyate ||
children.translated_text: One asks: even for fearless beings such as <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest, destruction is heard of at the cosmic dissolution.
Therefore it is not eternal merely because of fearlessness.
Or what is the defining mark of one who is fearless?
That is now stated.
Here the prefix a- negates destruction.

children.text: atra kṣayo nāma sati puruṣanityatve pūrvam asya brāhmaṇasya tais tair aiśvaryair apakarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here 'destruction,' while the person is admittedly eternal, means the diminution formerly suffered by this brāhmaṇa with respect to those various lordly powers.
Connection with what consists of ego, the great principle, and the like is impermanent.

children.text: ayaṃ tu anena nityena māheśvareṇaiśvaryeṇa yogāt puruṣaḥ akṣayaḥ ity upacaryate ||
children.translated_text: But because this person is connected with this eternal <s>Māheśvara</s> lordly power, he is figuratively called imperishable.
It is like a royal treasury or the wealth of a householder.

children.text: āha īśvarāṇām api yayātiprabhṛtīnāṃ jarābhibhavanād atha kim ayaṃ jīryate neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: since even lords such as <s>Yayāti</s> and others are overcome by old age, does this one age or not?
Or what is the defining mark of one who is imperishable?
That is now stated.
Here the prefix a- negates old age.

children.text: atra jarā nāma palitaskhalityādilakṣaṇā kāryasya dṛkkriyāśaktihāniś ca karaṇānām ||
children.translated_text: Here 'old age' means what is marked by grey hair, falling hair, and the like, and also the loss, in the instruments, of the powers of seeing and acting that belong to the body.
Why?
Because he experiences its result, he is figuratively said to age.

children.text: idānīṃ tu kāmitvād vikaraṇadharmitvāc ca nāstītyataḥ ajara ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: But now, because he has the faculty of willing and because he has the nature of being without instruments, that does not exist; therefore he is called ageless.

children.text: āha ajarāṇām api devādīnāṃ saṃhārād arvāṅ mṛtyur dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: One asks: even for ageless beings such as the gods and the rest, death is seen before the cosmic dissolution.

children.text: atha kim asya mṛtyur vidyate neti ||
children.translated_text: Then does death exist for this one or not?
Or what is the defining mark of one who is ageless?
That is now stated.
Here the prefix a- negates death.
The root mṛ means abandoning the breaths.
Here the cessation of the activity of the breaths and the like is called death.
Why?
Because he experiences its result.
For him, because he has the faculty of willing and because he has the nature of being without instruments, that does not exist; therefore,
he is called deathless.
Therefore it is established from statements such as 'fearless' and 'imperishable' that the lordly power is eternal.
One asks:

children.text: sarvatra abhipretārtheṣu pravartamānasya maheśvareṇāpi apratibandhadharmitvam apratīghātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In all desired objects toward which he proceeds, an absence of the property of being obstructed even by <s>Maheśvara</s> is non-frustration.

children.text: ity etaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ avaśyatvānāveśyatvāvadhyatvābhītatvākṣayatvājaratvāmaratvāpratīghātatvākhyaiḥ aṣṭabhir guṇaiḥ siddhilakṣaṇair yukto bhagavato mahādevasya mahāgaṇapatir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with these eight previously stated qualities, which are marks of accomplishment and are called not being subject to control, not being possessed, invulnerability, fearlessness, imperishability, agelessness, deathlessness, and non-frustration, he becomes the great <s>Gaṇapati</s> of the blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>.
His being superior to all bound beings is greatness, because of the excellence of his lordly power.
The gaṇas are <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and the others.
Lordship is mastery over all effects beginning with bound beings.
Having thus completed the chapter, it is proper to speak.

children.text: bṛhac ca tebhyaḥ sarvabrahmabhyaḥ svayaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And he himself becomes greater than all those brahmans.
And 'he should recite' is a mental action.
It should be understood as something to be recited.

children.text: uktam āha japayajñastu yajñānāṃ viśiṣṭo daśabhirguṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: A stated saying declares: among sacrifices, the sacrifice of recitation is distinguished by ten qualities.
Recitation in a low voice is a hundred times greater; mental recitation is remembered as a thousand times greater.
Therefore it should be recited with the mind alone.
If one asks, for what purpose?

children.text: taducyate adharmavyucchittyarthaṃ dharmasya cābhivṛddhyarthaṃ tasya cākuśalebhyo vyāvartanārthaṃ brahmaṇyanavaratapadapaṅktyām upanibandhanārthaṃ cetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is stated: the meaning is that it is for the removal of <s>adharma</s>, for the increase of <s>dharma</s>, for turning him away from unwholesome things, and for binding him constantly in the sequence of words belonging to brahman.
One asks: what, then, is that brahman?
Here the answer is: that which begins with <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Or else here there is a remote connection between the chapters on brahman and on study.
How?
When '<s>Paśupati</s>' is said, a doubt arises.

children.text: kiṃnarapatisurapatiprajāpatiprabhṛtivad asyaiśvaryaṃ kṛtam anityam āgantukaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Is his lordly power produced, impermanent, or adventitious, like that of a lord of Kinnaras, a lord of gods, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the like?

children.text: kiṃ cāsya janma mṛtyur vā vidyate neti ||
children.translated_text: And does birth or death exist for him or not?
The answer is: no.
Because he says:

children.text: atra sadyaḥ ity asmin pade 'rthadvayaṃ cintyate ||
children.translated_text: Here in the word '<s>sadyaḥ</s>' two meanings are to be considered:
existent and first.
As in the case of acquisition and protection.
Here '<s>sat</s>' is used in the sense of eternality.
Why?
Because there is no cause of destruction.

children.text: nityaṃ dhruvam avināśi patyuḥ patitvaṃ nānyeṣām ity ato'bhidhīyate sad iti ||
children.translated_text: The lordship of the Lord is eternal, fixed, and imperishable, and not that of others; therefore it is designated by '<s>sat</s>'.

children.text: āha kim ayam ādimattve sati nityo mokṣavat ||
children.translated_text: One asks: if he has a beginning, is he eternal, like liberation?
The answer is: no.
Because he says: first.
With respect to what is distinct from him.

children.text: hetor asaṃbhavād ādyaman āgantukaṃ patyuḥ patitvaṃ nānyeṣām ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because no cause is possible, the meaning is that the lordship of the Lord is first, not adventitious, and not that of others.

children.text: āha kiṃ nityānāditve sati puruṣavaj jāyate ||
children.translated_text: One asks: if he is eternal and beginningless, is he born like a person?
The answer is: no.
Because he says: unborn.
Here the prefix a- negates birth and death.
The blessed Lord, free from stain, is devoid of birth and death.
Why?
Because there is no obtaining of activity accompanied by stain.
Because freedom from self-conceit belongs to no others.
'Unborn' is the object.

children.text: āha athaitat sattvam ādyatvam ajātatvaṃ ca guṇaṃ kāraṇe jñātvā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: One asks: when the practitioner has understood being, primacy, and unbornness as a quality in the cause, what should he do?
That is stated: it is to be approached in surrender.
Because he says: I take refuge.
This is the instruction in the word of the practitioner.

children.text: yathā agne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: As in the expression, 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of the vow, I shall observe the vow.'

children.text: atra praśabdaḥ kāraṇāntareṣu sattvādyatvājātatvapratiṣedhārtho bhṛśārthaś ca ||
children.translated_text: Here the prefix <s>pra</s>, because it concerns other causes and because it is not the state of <s>sattva</s>, primordiality, or unbornness, has the purpose of negation, and it also has the sense of intensity.

children.text: tasmāt sarvabhāvānabhiṣvaṅgeṇa tad eva kāraṇaṃ prapattavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, without attachment to any beings, that very cause is to be resorted to.
The meaning is that it is to be accepted as refuge.
One asks: when one has taken refuge here, what will he do?
Or what will he give?

children.text: tad ucyate pūjāṃ kariṣyaty ātmānaṃ ca dāsyati ||
children.translated_text: That is answered: he will perform worship, and he will give himself.
As he says:

children.text: āha sattvam ādyatvam ajātatvaṃ ca pūrvoktam ||
children.translated_text: One asks: <s>sattva</s>, primordiality, and unbornness have been stated before.
In 'unto <s>Sadyojāta</s>,' the fourth case is used.
The word <s>vai</s> indicates affirmation.

children.text: sattvam ādyatvam ajātatvaṃ ca dharmān saṃbhāvya bravīti sadyo'jātāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having affirmed the qualities of <s>sattva</s>, primordiality, and unbornness, he says, 'Homage indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.'
The word <s>namaḥ</s> is used for giving oneself and for worship.

children.text: namaskāreṇātmānaṃ prayacchati pūjāṃ ca prayuṅkta ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that by the act of homage he gives himself and performs worship.

children.text: āha kiṃ prayojanam ātmānaṃ maheśvarāya prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: One asks: for what purpose does he give himself to <s>Maheśvara</s>?
Is there some suffering of his?
Or what does he seek from <s>Maheśvara</s>?

children.text: kiṃ vā svayam utpāditānugṛhītatirobhāvitānāṃ paśūnāṃ patiḥ uta parairiti ||
children.translated_text: Or is he himself the lord of the bound souls whom he has produced, favored, and concealed, or is he such because of others?
The answer is: by himself.
Because he says:
Here 'in being after being' is repetition.
The word <s>bhava</s> includes all of knowledge, the kalās, and the bound souls collectively.
Why is it called <s>bhava</s>?
Because it is made by coming-to-be and causing-to-be.
For the Lord makes them become gods, humans, and animals.
He is <s>Bhava</s> because <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, power, non-dharma, ignorance, attachment, and powerlessness are conditions of coming-to-be and causing-to-be.
Having seen his repeated production, favoring, and concealment of it,

children.text: vīpsāyāḥ utpattāv utpattāv anugrahe'nugrahe tirobhāve tirobhāve cety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the repetition means: in production after production, favor after favor, and concealment after concealment.
The phrase is 'not in excessive being.'
The negative particle denies the state of being an effect.
The meaning is: may I not exist among beings that are surpassed or excessive.

children.text: āha kiṃ bhavād viyogamātram evaikaṃ mṛgayate ||
children.translated_text: One asks: does he seek only separation from <s>bhava</s>?
That is answered: no.
Because he says:
Here <s>bhaja</s> means favoring.
<s>Sva</s> is a designation of the cause.
<s>Mām</s> is a designation of the self.

children.text: bhajasva māṃ trāyasva mām anugṛhṇīṣva māmityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: favor me, protect me, show grace to me.
One asks: whom does he address?
To whom does he resort?
To whom does he make homage?
Who, being such, liberates that person from <s>bhava</s>?
Or to whom does he say, 'favor me'?
That is answered, because he says:
Here the word <s>bhava</s> refers precisely to knowledge, the kalās, and the bound souls.
Because the blessed Lord is the producer of that, he is called <s>Bhavodbhava</s>, the source of <s>bhava</s>.

children.text: atrotpādakānugrāhakatirobhāvakadharmi kāraṇam utpādyānugrāhyatirobhāvyadharmi kāryam ityetat kāryakāraṇayor lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Here the cause has the properties of producing, favoring, and concealing, while the effect has the properties of being produced, favored, and concealed; this is the definition of cause and effect.
In regard to this cause, resorting and the other acts should be understood as useful in due sequence.

children.text: evamatra bhagavatkauṇḍinyakṛte pañcārthabhāṣye prathamo'dhyāyaḥ saha brahmaṇā granthato 'rthataśca parisamāpta iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Pañcārthabhāṣya</s> composed by the venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the first chapter, together with the Brahman, is completed both as to text and as to meaning.
The meaning is: the best by names.
For it has been said:
In standards, horns, offerings, ornaments, and marks of a person,
<s>Vāma</s> is stated in the meanings 'best,' 'not crooked,' and 'new.'
One asks: what is the motive for his activity of producing and the rest, or what purpose does it have?
That is answered:
Thus.
Here <s>deva</s> is from the verbal root <s>div</s>, 'to play.'
Because he has play as his property, play is its motive.

children.text: krīḍāvāneva sa bhagavān vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñakaṃ trividhamapi kāryam utpādayan anugṛhṇāti tirobhāvayati cety ato devaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since that blessed Lord, being possessed of play, produces, favors, and conceals the threefold effect called knowledge, kalā, and bound soul, he is therefore <s>Deva</s>.
His activity should be understood as having production and the like as its results.
In 'of <s>Deva</s>,' the genitive denotes possession of that property.

children.text: āha kiṃ nāmadvayamevātra kāraṇe vitanyate arthadvayameva vā āhosvid anyadapyasti neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: are only two names extended here in relation to the cause, or only two meanings, or is there something else too?
The answer is: there is.
Because he says:
Thus.
Here, because of supremacy, he is <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, the eldest or most excellent.
Over whom, and by what, is he supreme?
That is answered: over the perfected beings, the practitioners, and the bound souls.

children.text: tadāyattatvāt siddhasādhakabhāvasya sarvapaśūnāṃ ca pravṛttinivṛttisthityādiphalānām ityato jyeṣṭhaḥ parataraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the states of being perfected or a practitioner, and the results for all bound souls such as activity, cessation, and stability, depend on him, he is therefore <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, superior,
and the most superior.
And his sovereignty is uncreated.
For it has been said:
His power, characterized by vision and action, is the eternal property of the principle;
therefore he is the best among all beings, and for that reason he is remembered as supreme.
Thus, because of supremacy, he is <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>.
Here too, in 'of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>,' the genitive denotes possession of that property.

children.text: āha kiṃ nāmatrayam evātra kāraṇe cintyate arthatrayameva vā āhosvid anyadapyasti neti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: are only three names considered here in relation to the cause, or only three meanings, or is there something else too?
The answer is: there is.
Thus.

children.text: atra rutasya bhayasya drāvaṇāt saṃyojanād rudraḥ tatra rutam abhilāpa ityanarthāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Here, because he drives away and joins beings to crying, that is, fear, he is <s>Rudra</s>; in that expression, <s>ruta</s>, 'crying,' is not different in meaning from utterance.
Driving away is so called.
Fear is manifold.
For it has been said:
Because, by means of many kinds of created things and also by manifold fears,

children.text: saṃyojayati bhūtāni tasmād rudra iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he joins beings, therefore he is remembered as <s>Rudra</s>.
Here too the genitive denotes possession of that property.
One asks: what is that?
Or of what kind is that which belongs to him?
That is answered:

children.text: atra trividhena kāryeṇa vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñakena tatraiva sthityutpattipralayān prāpnuvatā kalitaṃ śobhitaśabditaṃ nabhastārābhir ivetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the threefold effect designated as <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>paśu</s>, which undergoes preservation, origination, and dissolution in that very [seat], it is "kalita," that is, adorned and called beautiful, like the sky with stars. This is the meaning.

children.text: āha yadetat patyuḥ patitvaṃ śaktiḥ sāmarthyamaiśvaryaṃ svaguṇaḥ sadbhāvaḥ satattvaṃ tattvadharmaḥ tad āsanam ||
children.translated_text: One asks: This lordship of the Lord, namely power, capacity, sovereignty, his own quality, true being, real essence, and the property of reality: that is the seat.
It is not a posture of sitting, like the lotus-seat. This is the meaning. Why is it called a seat?
That in which he sits is a seat.
Or the effect is occupied by him through this; therefore it is called a seat. This is the meaning.
Therefore it is a seat.

children.text: ato'vyayo'mṛto bhagavān kāmataḥ svaśaktisthaṃ kāryaṃ svaśaktyā adhyāste ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the imperishable, immortal <s>Bhagavān</s>, at will, by his own power occupies the effect that rests in his own power.
Therefore both effect and cause are situated in the seat.
One asks: there is the defect that the functions of effect and cause would be mixed, as with the milk of cows, goats, sheep, and buffaloes.
That is answered: no.
There is no mixture, as with the forms and other qualities at the tips of the fingers.
And there is no mixture, as with the light of a lamp and the sun and with the rays of the eye.

One asks: if there is mixture, there is the defect of non-delimitation among <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, and the <s>kalās</s>, as with substances such as <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>koṭa</s>.

children.text: taducyate ekottarotkarṣeṇa vyāpyavyāpakabhāvenāvasthitānāṃ tattvādīnāṃ nāparicchedadoṣaḥ sūtratvād vyāpakaṃ maheśvaratattvaṃ vyāpyaṃ puruṣādipañcaviṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: This is said: for the <s>tattvas</s> and the rest that are established by successive superiority, one above another, in the relation of pervaded and pervader, there is no defect of non-delimitation. Because it is like a thread, the <s>Maheśvara-tattva</s> is the pervader, while the twenty-five beginning with <s>puruṣa</s> are the pervaded.

children.text: tathā ātmatvād vyāpakaṃ puruṣatattvaṃ vyāpyaṃ pradhānādicaturviṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, because it has the nature of self, the <s>puruṣa-tattva</s> is the pervader, while the twenty-four beginning with <s>pradhāna</s> are the pervaded.
Likewise <s>pradhāna</s> is the pervader, while the twenty-three beginning with intellect are the pervaded.
Intellect is the pervader, while the twenty-two beginning with egoity are the pervaded.

children.text: tathā vyāpako bhavatyahaṃkāraḥ vyāpyānyekādaśendriyāṇi daśavidhaṃ ca kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise egoity is the pervader, while the eleven faculties and the tenfold effect are the pervaded.
The eleven faculties are the pervaders, while the five subtle elements, sound and the rest, are the pervaded.

children.text: tathā vyāpakāni pañcabhūtasūkṣmāṇi śabdādīni vyāpyāni ākāśādīni pañcamahābhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the five subtle elements, sound and the rest, are the pervaders, while the five great elements, space and the rest, are the pervaded.
Likewise space is the pervader, while the four elements beginning with wind are the pervaded.

children.text: tathā vyāpako bhavati vāyuḥ vyāpyaṃ tejaḥprabhṛti bhūtatrayam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise wind is the pervader, while the three elements beginning with fire are the pervaded.

children.text: tathā vyāpakaṃ bhavati tejaḥ vyāpyam abādidvayam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise fire is the pervader, while the pair beginning with water is the pervaded.
Likewise the waters are the pervaders, while earth is the pervaded.
Earth is the pervader, while the effects characterized as earth, water, and sap are the pervaded.

children.text: tathā vyāpakāni bhūmyudakarasalakṣaṇāni kāraṇāni vyāpyaṃ devamanuṣyatiryagyoni tṛṇauṣadhivṛkṣagulmalatāvanaspatyādikāryam anekavidham ato nāparicchedadoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the causes characterized as earth, water, and sap are the pervaders, while the many kinds of effects, namely gods, humans, animal wombs, grasses, herbs, trees, shrubs, creepers, forest trees, and so on, are the pervaded. Therefore there is no defect of non-delimitation.

children.text: āha vṛttyasaṃkaragrahaṇe dṛṣṭāntābhāvād ayuktam taducyate haridrodakavad vyāpyaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca tadyathā haridrodake snigdhatvaśaityādidharmair apāṃ grahaṇaṃ gandhavarṇaghanakṣāratvādibhir haridrāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: One asks: if non-mixture of functions is accepted, it is unreasonable because there is no example. This is said: as with turmeric-water, there is both the pervaded and the pervader. For example, in turmeric-water, water is apprehended by qualities such as smoothness and coolness, and turmeric by smell, color, thickness, acridity, and so on.
Likewise <s>Īśvara</s> is apprehended through the arrangement of places such as oceans and divine realms, bodies, faculties, objects, and the like, and through the conjunction of pleasure and pain.
The same applies also to <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: īśvarasyāpi apariṇāmidharmitvāt sukhaduḥkhadātṛtvāc ca pradhānadharmādharmādīnāṃ grahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: And even of <s>Īśvara</s>, because he is the bearer of unchanging properties and because he gives pleasure and pain, there is apprehension of <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the rest.

children.text: tathā pradhānasya mānasasaṃkalpālocanagamanādibhiḥ karaṇagrāmasya viṣayāṇāṃ ca grahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, of <s>pradhāna</s>, there is apprehension of the aggregate of instruments and of objects through mental resolve, reflection, movement, and so on.

children.text: tathā dhṛtisaṃgrahapaktivyūhāvakāśadānādibhir dharmaiḥ pṛthivyādīnāṃ grahaṇamiti pradhānavādino manyante ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, through properties such as firmness, cohesion, digestion, arrangement, and the granting of space, there is apprehension of earth and the other elements; so the proponents of <s>pradhāna</s> think.
One asks: then, in this <s>tantra</s>, how are effect and cause established?
That must be stated.

children.text: taducyate iha yasmād āha śarvasarvebhyaḥ iti vacanād yathāsambhavam ||
children.translated_text: This is said: here, because he says "from <s>Śarva</s> to all," it is according to what is possible.

children.text: sati vibhutve svavṛttyā kāryakāraṇayoḥ sarvagatatve'pi svavṛttyasaṃkaraḥ tasmād āsanasthaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: When omnipresence exists, even though effect and cause are all-pervading through their own functions, there is no mixture of their own functions. Therefore both effect and cause are situated in the seat.

children.text: āha kiṃ tad āsanasthaṃ kāryam āsane nityam āhosvid anityamiti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: is that effect situated in the seat eternal in the seat, or is it non-eternal?
It is said: the effect is eternal.
Why?
It belongs to the Lord.
Because the causal Lord is eternal, the Lord's status as <s>pati</s> is eternal.
Here, because of the statement beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the protector is eternal.
And because the protector is eternal, what is protected is also eternal.
Why?

children.text: na hy asati pālye pālaka ityeva ||
children.translated_text: For when there is no protected thing, there is simply no protector.
Since there is eternity, he joins those very things, the <s>paśus</s> and the rest.
This follows from the example of ramparts and the like made of clay and metal.
The obtaining of function is called origination.

Maintenance is favor, because the abodes such as place, body, faculty, and object mutually assist one another; favor is the favor impelled by <s>Īśvara</s>. Separation and the loss of function are also [to be understood].
Loss is non-existence.

children.text: tasmāt triṣvapi kāleṣu āsanasthaṃ kāryaṃ draṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore in all three times the effect should be understood as situated in the seat.
This means: like a seed in the earth.

children.text: āha kiṃ tat kāryaṃ bhagavān yugapadutpādayati kramaśo vā ||
children.translated_text: One asks: does <s>Bhagavān</s> produce that effect all at once or successively?
Or is he dependent on <s>karma</s>, or independent?
This is said: as he wishes.
For he says:
Here the word "all" should be understood as denoting, without remainder, the effect beginning with <s>vidyā</s>.
In the word "kāmika" here too, a triad is considered.

children.text: kāmī kāmaḥ kāmyamiti ca tatra kāmī īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Namely, the desirer, desire, and the desired; among these, the desirer is <s>Īśvara</s>.
His desire is his wish.
The desired is the effect beginning with <s>vidyā</s>.
He produces that either without sequence or sequentially, just as he wishes.
Why?
Because he acts by will.
And from this very fact his non-dependence on karma is established.

children.text: karmakāminaśca maheśvaramapekṣante na tu bhagavānīśvaraḥ karma puruṣaṃ vāpekṣate ||
children.translated_text: Those who desire karmic results depend on <s>Maheśvara</s>, but the blessed Lord, <s>Īśvara</s>, does not depend on karma or on a person.
Therefore <s>Īśvara</s> is not dependent on karma.
The word 'iti', since the meanings have been explained, serves to close the topic.
One objects: being possessed of desire would produce dissimilarity from the principle.

children.text: kāryatvena vā pariṇāmitvam ātmano bandhamokṣaviparyayaṃ vā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, through being an effect, it would make the self subject to transformation, or would make a reversal of bondage and liberation for the self.
That is answered, because he says 'āṅ'.

children.text: āṅ iti kāryakāraṇatvam ātmano muktānāṃ ca maryādā ||
children.translated_text: The syllable 'āṅ' indicates the relation of effect and cause, and the boundary of the self and of the liberated ones.

children.text: taducyate utpādyānugrāhyatirobhāvyakalpakatvābhāvakatvenāpariṇāmitvam ātmano muktānāṃ ca punarduḥkhair asaṃyojanam ityeṣā kāraṇamaryādā ||
children.translated_text: This is explained: by being the producer, favorer, concealer, and arranger, and not something produced, there is non-transformation of the self, and no renewed connection of the liberated ones with sufferings; this is the boundary of the cause.
And the boundary of the effect is to be established.
That is explained as the boundary of what is to be produced, favored, concealed, arranged, and modified.
And it is subject to another objection.
The root <s>cakṣiṅ</s> is used in the sense of telling.
It has been declared by the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, who exists for the effects.
The power of the blessed <s>Maheśvara</s> is eternal.
The meaning is that the effect beginning with knowledge has been fashioned by that power.
And likewise the meaning is, 'it has been described.'
Here this governing section on effect and cause is completed.
What, then, is being possessed of desire, and what is <s>Rudra</s>'s being possessed of desire?
Is just this the great excellence in the cause, or is there something else?
The answer is: there is.
Because he says:

children.text: amaṅgalam iti atra sādhanajātam adhikurute taduddeśena tu maṅgalavacananirdeśaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: In 'inauspicious', he here takes up the class of means; but with reference to that he gives an instruction expressed by the word 'auspicious'.
The word 'ca' should be understood as introducing a statement of the qualities of the cause.
Having introduced it, we shall later explain both auspiciousness and <s>pradakṣiṇa</s>, clockwise rightward movement.

children.text: tasmādubhayaṃ rudre devāśca pitaraśca ityupariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we shall state below that both, the gods and the ancestors, are in <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: atraśabde mūrtyadhiṣṭhātari manaḥsaṃjñe kāraṇe sakale upatiṣṭhatā apasavyasambandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
