children.text: āha ṛṣitvaṃ vipratvaṃ ca kīdṛśe maheśvare cintanīyam ||
children.translated_text: One asks: In what sort of <s>Maheśvara</s> are ṛṣi-hood and vipra-hood to be contemplated?
Or what sort of <s>oṃkāra</s> is to be meditated upon?
That is stated.
Here also 'pure in speech' is another name of the Blessed Lord.
'Not these' means that the Blessed Lord is other than them.

children.text: sa yathā hy atho hitvā vāṇīṃ manasā saha rūparasagandhavidyāpuruṣādiparo niṣkalo dhyeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For just so, having abandoned speech together with the mind, he is to be meditated on as partless and beyond form, taste, smell, knowledge, person, and the like.
Because it has been said:

children.text: ākṛtimapi parihṛtya dhyānaṃ nityaṃ pare rudre
children.translated_text: Even having put aside form, there is constant meditation on the supreme <s>Rudra</s>;

children.text: yena prāptaṃ yoge muhūrtamapi tat paro yogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when that has been attained in yoga even for a moment, that is the highest yoga.
The meaning is: the supreme yoga.

children.text: āha atha yathāyaṃ bālavan niṣkalastathā kiṃ samānapuruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One asks: Now, since this one is partless in this way, like a child, is he a person of the same kind?
It is said: no.
Because he says, 'even then this one.'

children.text: atrānādyajñānadyatinā ṛṣitvavipratvasaṃjñakena mahatā aiśvaryeṇa maheśvara iti siddham iha tu yadāyaṃ vāgviśuddho niṣkalastadā kiṃ samānapuruṣavad anīśvara ityasya saṃśayasya saṃvyudāsārtham ucyate maheśvara iti ||
children.translated_text: Here the designation <s>Maheśvara</s> has been established by the great lordship, called ṛṣi-hood and vipra-hood, consisting in beginningless knowledge and activity. But here, when this one is pure in speech and partless, the term <s>Maheśvara</s> is stated in order to remove the doubt, 'Is he powerless, like an ordinary person?'

children.text: yasmād asyaiśvaryaṃ niṣkalasyāpi svaguṇasadbhāvaḥ satattvaṃ tattvadharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For lordship, even in the case of the partless one, is the existence of his own quality, his real nature, and an essential property.
Its being unmade is like the consciousness of the person.
Therefore even then this one is great, indeed the Lord, <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tasmādakṛtaka eva mahacchabda ityato maheśvara iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the word 'great' itself is unmade; hence he is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Thus the object to be meditated on has been stated as the <s>oṃkāra</s>.
The characterization of the qualities of the object of meditation has been stated in 'this one is an ṛṣi, a vipra, and great.'
The determination of the object of meditation has been stated in 'pure in speech' and 'partless.'
And the praise of the power of the object of meditation has been stated in '<s>Maheśvara</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ yasmād indriyajaye vartate ato vasatyarthavṛttibalakriyālābhādayaśca vyākhyātā iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because he is engaged in the conquest of the senses, residence, livelihood, strength, practice, attainments, and the rest have been explained.
Therefore it is proper to say here:
The section on the empty house and cave is complete.

children.text: āha śūnyāgāraguhāyāṃ yadā jitānīndriyāṇi devanityatā ca prāptā bhavati tadā kiṃ tadeva bhaikṣyaṃ vṛttimāsthāya tatraivānena duḥkhāntaprāpteḥ stheyam ||
children.translated_text: One asks: When the senses have been conquered in the empty house or cave and divine permanence has been attained, should this person remain right there, adopting that same livelihood of begging, until the attainment of the end of suffering?
Or are visible purposes also seen for his residence, livelihood, strength, practices, and attainments?
It is answered: they are seen.
Because he says:

children.text: āha śūnyāgāraguhām utsṛjya prayojanābhāvāt śmaśāne saṃkrāntirayukteti cet ||
children.translated_text: One asks: If, after leaving the empty house and cave, moving to a cremation ground is improper because there is no purpose,
it is said: no.
Because its purpose is the removal of attachment to yoga.

children.text: ihāvasthānād avasthānaṃ prāpya brāhmaṇasya sarvatra vasatyarthavṛttibalakriyālābhādayo 'yutasiddhā vaktavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After obtaining one mode of abiding after another by staying here, residence everywhere, livelihood, strength, practices, attainments, and so on are to be stated for the Brahmin as inseparably established.

children.text: tatrādidharmā apyasya tāvadāyatane vasatyarthaḥ vṛttirbhaikṣyaṃ balamaṣṭāṅgaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kriyāḥ sthānahasitādyāḥ snānaṃ kaluṣāpohaḥ śuddhiḥ jñānāvāptiḥ akaluṣatvaṃ ca lābhā iti ||
children.translated_text: There, among his first dharmas, first, in a temple the purpose of residence is dwelling; the livelihood is begging; the strength is eight-limbed celibacy; the practices are standing, laughing, and the like; bathing is the removal of impurity; purity, acquisition of knowledge, and freedom from impurity are the attainments.

children.text: tathā asanmānaparibhavopadeśād āyatane vasatyarthaḥ vṛttirutsṛṣṭaṃ balamakaluṣatvam indriyadvārapidhānaṃ ca kriyā indriyāṇi pidhāya unmattavadavasthānaṃ pāpakṣayāc chuddhiḥ lābhastu kṛtsno dharmas tulyendriyajaye vartate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, because disrespect, insult, and admonition are taught, in the temple the purpose of residence is staying there; the livelihood is discarded food; the strength is freedom from impurity and closing the doors of the senses; the practices are remaining like a madman after closing the senses; purity comes from the destruction of evil, while the attainment is the whole dharma, which is engaged in equal conquest of the senses.

children.text: tathā vasatyarthaḥ śūnyāgāraguhā vṛttirbhaikṣyaṃ balaṃ gomṛgayoḥ sahadharmitvaṃ kriyā adhyayanadhyānādyā ajitendriyavṛttitāpohaḥ śuddhiḥ lābhastu devanityatā jitendriyatvaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, the meaning of residence is an empty house or a cave; livelihood is alms; strength is having a common property with cows and deer; the practices are study, meditation, and so on; purity is the removal of the distress belonging to the conduct of one whose senses are not conquered; and the benefit is divine permanence and conquest of the senses.
So too here, in the expression "dwelling in a cremation ground," the meaning is residence: by dwelling there he is one whose self is <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yathālabdhamiti vṛttiḥ kriyā smṛtiḥ asmṛtyapohaḥ śuddhiḥ lābhastu sāyujyam ||
children.translated_text: "According to what is obtained" means livelihood; the practice is remembrance; purity is the removal of non-remembrance; and the benefit is <s>sāyujya</s>.

children.text: tathottaratra ṛṣir iti vasatyarthaḥ balamapramādaḥ prasāda upāyaḥ duḥkhāpohaḥ śuddhiḥ guṇāvāptiśca lābha iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the later expression "the seer," the meaning is residence; strength is freedom from negligence; grace is the means; purity is the removal of suffering; and the benefit is the attainment of the qualities.
And so it has been said:

children.text: pañca lābhān malān pañca pañcopāyān viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever understands, in particular, the five benefits, the five impurities, and the five means,

children.text: yastu budhyati pañcārthe sa vidvān nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is learned in the five objects; there is no doubt about this.
The first benefit is the gain of knowledge, then the gain of austerity and divine permanence;
yoga and the manifestation of the qualities are to be known here as the five benefits.
Ignorance, <s>adharma</s>, repeated practice of sense-objects, failure to attain steadiness,

children.text: anaiśvaryaṃ ca malā vijñeyāḥ pañca pañcārthe ||
children.translated_text: and lack of mastery are to be known as the five impurities in the Pañcārtha system.
Residence, meditation, complete restraint of all the instruments, and also remembrance,

children.text: prasāda iti copāyā vijñeyāḥ pañca pañcārthe ||
children.translated_text: together with grace, are to be known as the five means in the Pañcārtha system.

children.text: vāsārtho lokaśca śūnyāgāraṃ tathā śmaśānaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The world as the place of residence, the empty house, and likewise the cremation ground,
and <s>Rudra</s>: these five places are definitely taught for the sake of accomplishment.
Therefore what was said is appropriate.

children.text: sa eva prāguktaḥ sambandhaḥ śmaśānavāsī iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the very connection stated earlier in the expression "one who dwells in a cremation ground."

children.text: atra śmaśānaṃ nāma yad etal lokādiprasiddhaṃ laukikānāṃ mṛtāni śavāni parityajanti tat ||
children.translated_text: Here, "cremation ground" means that place which is well known among ordinary people, where they abandon dead corpses.

children.text: śavasambandhāt śmaśānam tasminn ākāśe vṛkṣamūle yathānabhiṣvaṅgamaryādayā jitadvaṃdvena smṛtikriyāniviṣṭena vastavyam ||
children.translated_text: Because of its connection with corpses it is a cremation ground. In that place, whether in the open air or at the root of a tree, one should dwell according to the rule of non-attachment, with the pairs of opposites conquered and intent upon remembrance and practice.
Because of the connection with dwelling, he becomes a "dweller in a cremation ground," just as one may be a dweller on a sandbank: this is the meaning.
One asks: is his strength simply having a common property with cows and deer?
That is answered: no.
Because he says:

children.text: atra dharmo nāma ya eṣa yamaniyamapūrvako 'bhivyakto māhātmyādidharmaḥ sa pūrvoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>dharma</s> means that previously stated <s>dharma</s>, consisting in greatness and the like, manifested after the restraints and observances.
That has been accumulated in his own self.
Through that <s>dharma</s> he becomes one whose self is <s>dharma</s>: this is the meaning.
One asks: is alms alone his livelihood?
The answer is: no.
Because he says:

children.text: atra yathā iti samānārthe amlādiṣu jitendriyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here "as" is in the sense of equality, since the senses have been conquered in relation to sour things and the like.
"Obtained" means acquired, not asked for: this is the meaning.
The prefix upa is used in the sense of holding near.

children.text: tad yathālabdhamannapānaṃ śmaśānādanirgacchatā divase divase jīvanāya sthityarthaṃ tadupajīvan yathālabdhopajīvako bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, without leaving the cremation ground, day by day he lives on whatever food and drink has been obtained, for the sake of life and bodily maintenance; living on that, he becomes one who lives on what is obtained: this is the meaning.

children.text: āha kiṃ jīvanameva paro lābha iti ||
children.translated_text: One asks: is mere living the highest benefit?
The answer is: no.
Because he says:

children.text: atra labhate vindate āsādayatītyarthaḥ rudra iti kāraṇāpadeśe ||
children.translated_text: Here "he obtains" means he finds or acquires; the word <s>Rudra</s> is an indication of the cause.
The Rudra-hood of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated earlier.
Direct conjunction with <s>Rudra</s> is <s>sāyujya</s>.
The mention of "state" is meant to exclude anything other than the self and the Lord.
The completeness of yoga is <s>sāyujya</s>; thus it is understood as a synonym of yoga.
Because of the statement "one whose self is <s>dharma</s>," the sense is like transcendence and infinitude.
One asks: by what means does he obtain that?
Is it only by study and teaching?
That is answered: no.
Because he says:

children.text: atra sadā nityaṃ satatam avyucchinnamiti rudramiti kāraṇāpadeśe ||
children.translated_text: Here "always" means eternally, constantly, without interruption; the word <s>Rudra</s> is an indication of the cause.
The Rudra-hood of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated earlier.
"Rudra" is in the accusative, as the object.
The particle anu is used for an action performed after or following.
The previously stated object of meditation is to be remembered constantly.
Remembrance is a form of thought.
For the destruction of karma that remains like heat and is the cause of falling away, it is to be remembered constantly.
Remembrance, then, means divine permanence: this is the meaning.

children.text: tataḥ kṣīṇe karmaṇi taddoṣahetujālamūlaviśiṣṭasya pratyāsaikanimittābhāvāt sāyujyaprāptau na punaḥ saṃsāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that karma has been destroyed, because there is no single proximate cause belonging to one distinguished by the root of the network of causes of its defects, once <s>sāyujya</s> has been attained, there is no further transmigration.
Here the verse is explanatory.
One asks: because there may be extension and expansion of the involvement of ignorance, impurity, sin, latent impressions, and so on, there is a doubt.

children.text: sūkṣmavadavasthite karmaṇi kṣīṇe 'tyantaviśuddhaḥ sāyujyamāsādayati āhosvid aviśuddha iti ||
children.translated_text: When karma, remaining in a subtle state, has been destroyed, does he attain <s>sāyujya</s> as one who is utterly purified, or as one who is impure?
The answer is: as one who is purified.
Because he says:
Here, because it is stated out of order, "cutting" must be connected in sequence.
The cutting should be understood as consisting of restraint and holding fast.
For what purpose?
For the destruction of karma that remains in a subtle state, since the instruction beginning with residence has that purpose.

children.text: kiṃca arthānām anirvacanārthatvāt tatra japa eva kevalo'bhihitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, because the objects cannot be fully defined, there only recitation alone has been stated.

children.text: iha tu yata indriyāṇi jetavyāni yo jetā yayā jetavyāni yathā jetavyāni yatprayojanaṃ jetavyāni yasmiṃśca jite jitāni bhavanti tad vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But here we shall state why the senses are to be conquered, who the conqueror is, by what they are to be conquered, how they are to be conquered, for what purpose they are to be conquered, and in what, when it has been conquered, they are conquered.
Likewise we shall state whose self-conduct, study, meditation, remembrance, and the like are meant.

children.text: tathā yata ātmā chettavyaḥ chettāraṃ chedakaraṇaṃ chedaprayojanaṃ chedyaṃ chittiṃ yasmin chinne chinnaṃ bhavati tad vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise we shall state why the self is to be cut, the cutter, the instrument of cutting, the purpose of cutting, what is to be cut, the cutting, and in what, when it has been cut, the cutting is accomplished.
That is stated by the word "having cut."
Here "cutting" means simply the separation from identification with the condition of selfhood.
This is understood from the statement about cutting off.
By the word "tvā," one understands study, meditation, retention, restraint, and the like for one staying in an empty house or cave.
He asks: what is that?
Or, from what things is it to be cut off?
That is stated: it is the root of the network of causes of the faults.
Here the faults are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell.
Why?
Because they are the root of desire, acquisition, and the rest.
For it has been said:

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho bhayaṃ svapnaśca pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, likewise greed, fear, and sleep as the fifth,
attachment, hatred, and delusion.
Likewise there are faults such as acquisition, guarding, loss, attachment, and injury.
Acquisition means the means by which householders acquire objects, such as accepting gifts, conquest, buying, selling, investment, and so on.

children.text: eteṣu ca viṣayāṇāmarjane vartatātmapīḍā parapīḍā vā avarjanīye bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when one engages in acquiring these objects, injury to oneself or injury to another becomes unavoidable.

children.text: tatra yadyātmānaṃ pīḍayati tena ihaiva loke duḥkhī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: There, if one injures oneself, then one becomes miserable in this very world.

children.text: syāt paraṃ pīḍayati tatrāpyasyādharmo duḥkhādiphalaḥ saṃcīyate ||
children.translated_text: If one injures another, then in that case too <s>adharma</s>, whose fruit is suffering and the like, accumulates for him.
And that suffering is not experienced by someone else; the doer alone experiences it.
Moreover, sense-objects are like the fruits of the kimpāka tree.

children.text: tadyathā śrūyate lavaṇasāgarasaṃnikarṣe kālayavanadvīpe kimpākā nāma viṣavṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is heard that near the salt ocean, on the island of <s>Kālayavana</s>, there are poisonous trees called kimpākas.

children.text: tatphalāny āsvādenāmṛtopamāni ca kecidajñānād guḍavad bhakṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: Their fruits are like nectar in taste, and some people, through ignorance, eat them as if they were molasses.

children.text: bhakṣitāni ca tāni mūrchāṃ chardiṃ ca janayanti ||
children.translated_text: And when eaten, they produce fainting and vomiting.
Overcome by that intense suffering, they meet death.

children.text: śrutvā tu suhṛdāṃ vākyaṃ yo naro hy avamanyate
children.translated_text: But the person who, having heard the words of friends, disregards them
is burned at the end of ripening, like kimpāka fruits that have been eaten.

children.text: evaṃ kimpākaphalopamā viṣayāḥ sevyamānāḥ sukhaṃ janayanti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, sense-objects, like kimpāka fruits, produce pleasure while they are being enjoyed.
But in their outcome, because they are the cause of birth in saṃsāra, they lead to suffering.

children.text: ityevaṃ viṣayāṇāmarjane doṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood the fault in the acquisition of objects, perhaps one person among hundreds or thousands becomes detached.
Then how does another do so?
Let this be the fault in the acquisition of sense-objects.
Let it apply to them.
We do not deny that.
But there is another painful fault of sense-objects.
What is that?
It is stated: the fault of guarding them.

children.text: arjitānām apyeṣām avaśyam evodyatāyudhena rakṣā vidhātavyā ||
children.translated_text: Even after these objects have been acquired, they must necessarily be protected by one with weapon raised.
Why?
Because their fruits are shared with kings, fire, thieves, and heirs.
There there is injury to oneself.
And in injury to another, the result is as already stated.
For it has been said:
Just as thieves torment a man over his own property, and flesh-eaters torment him over his own flesh,

children.text: kleśayanti yathā ghorās tathāhi viṣayā naram ||
children.translated_text: so indeed terrible sense-objects torment a man.
And he experiences affliction from the possession of sense-objects;
from the abandonment of those very objects there would be the destruction of all affliction.
For the sake of removing the suffering of the self, one should practice the dharma of renunciation;
without abandoning sense-objects, a man devoted to sense-objects does not prosper in happiness.

children.text: viṣayāṇāmarjanādau doṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit ||
children.translated_text: Having understood the fault in the acquisition and other dealings with sense-objects, perhaps one person among hundreds or thousands becomes detached.
Then how does another do so?
Let these two faults, acquisition and guarding, belong to those sense-objects.
We do not deny them.

children.text: ayaṃ tv anyaḥ kaṣṭataro viṣayāṇāṃ doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But there is another still more painful fault of sense-objects.
What is that?
It is stated: the fault of loss.
Even when these objects have been acquired and well protected, their loss must necessarily be accepted.
And when sense-objects are lost, intense suffering again becomes manifest for those attached to sense-objects.

children.text: matsyādivad yathodakakṣaye nadīnāṃ tadvat tasmād aśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: Just like fish and other creatures when the water of rivers is exhausted, so it is; therefore this is not good.
For it has been said:
There are only three dangerous pools, carrying away all beings:
women, food and drink, and sovereignty; be watchful in regard to them, brahmins.
There is no eye equal to knowledge; there is no enemy equal to anger;

children.text: nāsti lobhasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgāt paraṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: there is no suffering equal to greed; there is no happiness higher than renunciation.
Thus.

children.text: evaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ kṣayadoṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit ||
children.translated_text: In this way, having understood the fault of the loss of sense-objects, perhaps one person among hundreds or thousands becomes detached.
Then how does another do so?
Let these faults of sense-objects exist.
There is another still more painful fault; what is it?
It is stated: the fault of attachment.

children.text: yadi tāvad arjanaṃ kriyate rakṣaṇaṃ ca kṣaye ca punaḥ punararjanaṃ kriyate rakṣaṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: If acquisition is undertaken, and guarding as well, and upon loss acquisition and guarding are again and again undertaken,
then the fault of attachment would not exist.
How so?

children.text: yāvad ayam indriyayukto viṣayān abhilaṣati tāvadasya tṛptirupaśāntirautsukyavinivṛttiśca na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: As long as this person, endowed with the senses, desires sense-objects, so long there is no satisfaction, no tranquillity, and no cessation of eagerness for him.
He begins again to seek still more sense-objects.
Then dissatisfaction and the rest arise again, just as before.
Therefore this is not good.
For it has been said:

children.text: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānām upabhogena śāmyati
children.translated_text: Desire is never appeased by the enjoyment of desired objects;
like the black-tracked fire by an oblation, it only increases all the more.

children.text: yat pṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever rice and barley, gold, cattle, and women there are on the earth,

children.text: nālamekasya tat tṛptyai tasmād vidvān śamaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: that is not enough for the satisfaction of one man; therefore the wise man should go to tranquillity.
Thus.

children.text: evaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ saṅgadoṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit ||
children.translated_text: In this way, having understood the fault of attachment to sense-objects, perhaps one person among hundreds or thousands becomes detached.
Then how does another do so?
Let these faults of sense-objects, beginning with acquisition, exist.
Let them apply to those objects.
We do not deny them.

children.text: ayaṃ tv anyaḥ kaṣṭatamo viṣayāṇāṃ doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But there is another, most painful fault of sense-objects.
And what is that?
It is stated: the fault of <s>hiṃsā</s> (injury).

children.text: śakyameteṣāṃ viṣayāṇām arjanādi kartum indriyalaulyadoṣo'pi bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: It may be possible to perform the acquisition and the like of these sense-objects; let there even be the fault of sensual restlessness of the senses.
If there were no fault of injury,
how so?

children.text: eteṣāmeva viṣayāṇāmupabhoge vartatā avaśyameva hiṃsādidoṣāḥ kartavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one who is engaged in the enjoyment of these very sense-objects, faults beginning with injury must necessarily be committed.
Why?
The enjoyment of sense-objects cannot be carried out without harming living beings.
Among them, first, this is done on account of sound.

children.text: tadyathā vīṇānimittaṃ khadirādīn chidyamānān dṛṣṭvā tantrīnimittaṃ vā kāṃściddhiṃsyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate kadanaṃ karma kriyate sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam ||
children.translated_text: For example, when someone sees khadira trees and the like being cut down for the sake of a vīṇā, or certain beings being injured for the sake of strings, if he should say, 'This killing of beings is not good; a cruel act is being done,' he should be told, 'In this matter, this is not unbecoming for you.'

children.text: yadā bhikṣāpradagṛheṣu ramyān śabdān śroṣyasi tatra paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When you hear pleasant sounds in the houses of almsgivers, there your supreme satisfaction will arise.
Likewise, first, killing of beings is done on account of thread and the like.

children.text: tadyathā kośakārādīn vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kadanaṃ karma kriyate ||
children.translated_text: For example, when someone sees silkworms and the like being killed, if he should say, 'This killing of beings is not good; a cruel act is being done,'

children.text: sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam yadā bhikṣadagṛheṣu mṛdutarasparśāni vāsāṃsi prāpsyasi tatra te paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: he should be told, 'In this matter, this is not unbecoming for you. When you obtain garments of very soft touch in the houses of almsgivers, there your supreme satisfaction will arise.'
Likewise, first, killing of beings is done on account of form.

children.text: tadyathā aśokādīn vṛkṣān chidyamānāndṛṣṭvā hastinaśca dantanimittaṃ vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano 'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kadanaṃ karma kriyate sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam ||
children.translated_text: For example, when someone sees aśoka trees and the like being cut down, and elephants being killed for the sake of ivory, if he should say, 'This killing of beings is not good; a cruel act is being done,' he should be told, 'In this matter, this is not unbecoming for you.'

children.text: yadā bhikṣadagṛham alaṃkṛtakavāṭagopuraṃ drakṣyasi tatra te paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When you see the house of an almsgiver with ornamented doors and gateways, there your supreme satisfaction will arise.
Likewise, first, killing of beings is done on account of taste.

children.text: tadyathā tittirimayūravarāhādīn vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano 'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: For example, when someone sees partridges, peacocks, boars, and the like being killed, if he should say, 'This killing of beings is not good,'
he should be told, 'In this matter, this is not unbecoming for you.'

children.text: yadā bhikṣadagṛheṣu ṣaḍrasamāṃsaprakārair bhokṣyase tatra te paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When you eat in the houses of almsgivers with six tastes and varieties of meat, there your supreme satisfaction will arise.
Likewise, first, killing of beings is done on account of smell.

children.text: tadyathā pañcanakhādīn vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kadanaṃ karma kriyate ||
children.translated_text: For example, when someone sees five-clawed animals and the like being killed, if he should say, 'This killing of beings is not good; a cruel act is being done,'
he should be told, 'In this matter, this is not unbecoming for you.'

children.text: yadā bhikṣadagṛheṣu sugandhān gandhān prāpsyasi tatra te paritoṣo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When you obtain fragrant scents in the houses of almsgivers, there your satisfaction will arise.
Thus:

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca bhayaṃ svapnaśca pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, greed, fear, and sleep as the fifth,
passion, hatred, and delusion,
so it is said.
Because they are rooted in acquisition, protection, loss, attachment, injury, and the like, therefore here sound and the other sense-objects are faults.
And in what way are they faults?
In the distraction of the mind.
They are <s>doṣas</s> (faults) because they corrupt.

children.text: dūṣayanti yasmād adhyayanadhyānādiniṣṭhaṃ sādhakaṃ vicittaṃ kurvantīti doṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because they corrupt a practitioner who is devoted to study, meditation, and the like, making him distracted, they are faults.
'Of the faults' is the genitive plural.

children.text: āha kiṃ doṣāṇāmeva doṣebhya eva vā chettavyamuktam ||
children.translated_text: He asks: has it been said that only the faults are to be cut off, or that one is to be cut off from the faults?
No.
For he states the cause.
Here the cause is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
Why?

children.text: cittacyutihetutvāt yasmāt tenāviṣṭaḥ sādhako 'dhyayanasmaraṇādibhyaś cyavatītyato 'trādharmo hetuḥ dharmastu sthityādihetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it is the cause of falling away of the mind: since a practitioner possessed by it falls away from study, recollection, and the like, therefore here <s>adharma</s> is the cause, while <s>dharma</s> is the cause of stability and the like.
He asks: of what is this the cause?
It is stated: of the net.

children.text: atra yadā adharmaḥ kūṭastho 'nārabdhakāryas tadā heturityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, when <s>adharma</s> is fixed and has not begun its effect, it is called the cause.

children.text: yadā tv ajñānavāsanāvaśāddhṛtyā sthityādibhāvam āpannastadā jālākhyāṃ labhate ||
children.translated_text: But when, under the influence of the impression of ignorance, it has attained the condition of stability and the like through persistence, then it receives the name 'net.'
Why?
The meaning is: of an aggregate like a net and the like.
Because there is no other cause made of that.
The genitive in 'of the net' is used with reference to the remaining act of cutting.
Therefore it is indeed cut.
Why?
Because the cause and the net arise from the conjunction of fault and mind.
He asks: what related thing becomes connected with fault, cause, and net?
Then how is it designated?
It is stated: the root.
Here, when 'root' is mentioned, the question arises: of what?
Because the cause and the net arise from the conjunction of fault and mind, and because of activity, it is understood from this that here the root is precisely the root of conjunction.
He asks: by what does this cutter perform the cutting of the root?
That is stated.
The intellect called the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument) has been mentioned.

children.text: tayā dharmasmṛticodanādisahitayā vidyāgṛhītayā buddhyā chedyaṃ sthāpyaṃ cetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that intellect, accompanied by <s>dharma</s>, memory, injunction, and the like, and grasped by knowledge, it is to be cut and established; this is the meaning.
He asks: although it is separated from killing and the like that accompany faults and so on, is that still called dependent on another?
No.
For he says: when what is called the root has ceased.

children.text: atra sam iti doṣādiviśliṣṭaṃ svayameva svaguṇatvena parigṛhyate agnyuṣṇatvavadity ānubandhitvāc cetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here 'sam' means that, separated from faults and the like, it is accepted by itself as possessing its own quality, like the heat of fire, and because it remains connected; this is the meaning.
He asks: what is that?
It is stated: <s>citta</s> (mind).

children.text: atra citī saṃjñāne cetayati cinoti vā aneneti cittam ||
children.translated_text: Here, from 'citi,' meaning consciousness: that by which one is conscious, or by which one gathers, is <s>citta</s>.

children.text: cetayati sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ padārthān cinoti dharmādharmau arjayatītyataḥ cetayati cinoti vā aneneti cittam ||
children.translated_text: Because by it one is conscious of pleasure and pain, gathers objects, and acquires <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, therefore <s>citta</s> is that by which one is conscious or by which one gathers.
<s>Citta</s> means mind, the inner organ.

children.text: atra tv etebhyo doṣahetutvādibhyo yugapac chettavyaṃ vidyamānebhyastu kramaśaḥ kṣapaṇamiti ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, because these faults and causes and the like are to be cut off all at once, while they are present their gradual destruction is intended.

children.text: āha chittvā tac cittaṃ kiṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: He asks: once that mind has been cut off, what is to be done?
The answer is: it is to be fixed in <s>Rudra</s>.
For he says:
Here the root sthā is used in the sense of cessation of movement.
The mind's absence of separation from <s>Rudra</s> is called steadiness.
The word vā indicates the completion of the act of recollection for one situated in a cremation ground and the like.
The word ca has the sense of conjunction.

children.text: na kevalaṃ chittvā stheyaṃ kiṃtu sthāpayitavyaṃ cetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that one should not only stand after cutting off the mind, but should also cause it to stand firm.
The word rudre is an indication of the cause.

children.text: rudrasya rudratvaṃ pūrvoktam rudra ityaupaśleṣikaṃ saṃnidhānam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudra</s>-ness of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated before; the word <s>Rudra</s> denotes close conjunction and nearness.
The mind is to be closely joined to <s>Rudra</s>, not to anything else: this is the meaning.
In this way mastery of the senses over their objects is to be accomplished.
Here the conqueror is the self.
That by which they are to be conquered is the intellect.
How they are to be conquered is gradually.
For what purpose they are to be conquered is for the sake of the mind's steadiness.

children.text: yasmiṃśca jite jitāni bhavanti cittam ityetadapi vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: And that in which, when it is conquered, they become conquered is the mind: this too has been explained.
The same should also be applied to cutting and the rest whose nature is muttering, restraint, and concentration.

children.text: tathāntaḥkaraṇavṛttim āsthāya kālaviśeṣanimittaraśmimaṇidīpavat tathātmavṛttiradhyayanadhyānasmaraṇādīni cittasthitiśca vyākhyātā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, by taking up the function of the inner organ, like a ray, a jewel, or a lamp conditioned by a particular time, the function of the self, study, meditation, recollection, and so on, and the steadiness of the mind have been explained.
The verse is etymological explanation.

children.text: āha kāryakaraṇaṃ ca tac cittasthitisamakālam eva rudre sthitāni tāni yuktāni ||
children.translated_text: He asks: when the effect and the instrument are also situated in <s>Rudra</s> at the very same time as the steadiness of the mind, are they joined?

children.text: atha kiṃ tānyeva yuktasya lakṣaṇāni iti ||
children.translated_text: Then are those very things the marks of one who is disciplined?
The answer is: no.
For he says:

children.text: atra dharmādharmayor vṛttyoruparame avasitaprayojanatvāt pakvaphalavat sarpakañcukavad gataprāyeṣu kāryakaraṇeṣu rudre sthitacitto niṣkala eka ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, when the activities of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> have ceased because their purpose has been completed, and when the effect and the instrument are nearly gone, like a ripe fruit or like a snake's slough, one whose mind is fixed in <s>Rudra</s> is said to be partless and one.

children.text: tathā yogavyāsaṅgakare 'dharme nivṛtte doṣādiviśliṣṭo nistīrṇakāntāravad avasthito rudre sthitacittaḥ kṣemī ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when <s>adharma</s>, which causes distraction from yoga, has ceased, one whose mind is fixed in <s>Rudra</s>, separated from faults and the like and standing as one who has crossed a wilderness, is called secure.

children.text: tathā sūkṣmasthūlasabāhyābhyantarasalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇāsu kriyāsu vinivṛttāsu rudre sthitacitto niṣkriyaḥ san ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when actions subtle and gross, external and internal, similar and dissimilar, have come to an end, one whose mind is fixed in <s>Rudra</s>, being inactive, is so described.
He asks: then how is it understood that this one is inactive?
And are there only these three marks of the disciplined person here?
The answer is: no.
For he says: free from sorrow.
Here sorrow is not different in meaning from anxious thought.
And that anxious thought is of two kinds.
It is wholesome and unwholesome.
Among these, the wholesome is study, meditation, recollection, and so forth.
The unwholesome is non-study, non-meditation, non-recollection, and so forth.

children.text: evaṃ japayantraṇadhāraṇādīṃśca kariṣyāmi na kariṣyāmītyevam anekavidhāyāmapi cintāyāṃ vinivṛttāyāṃ vyapagataśoko vītaśoka ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: When thought, even in its many forms such as 'I shall perform muttering, restraint, concentration, and the like' or 'I shall not perform them,' has completely ceased, one whose sorrow has gone away is called free from sorrow.
Thus the meaning of the term yoga is completed here.
Why?
Because the meanings have been explained etymologically.

children.text: yasmād asyādhyāyasyādāv uddiṣṭā ye padārthāste doṣacchedāsaṅgasthityādiṣu vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the topics that were stated at the beginning of this chapter have been explained in the cutting off of faults, non-attachment, steadiness, and so on.

children.text: evamanena yuktena brahmādayo devā viśeṣitā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this disciplined state, gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> are shown to be distinguished.
Because non-attachment and the like are taught for that.

children.text: āha atha sāṃkhyayogamuktāḥ kiṃ na viśeṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He asks: then are those liberated by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and Yoga not distinguished?
The answer is: they are distinguished.
How?
Because of the excellence of his knowledge over theirs.
How?
Those liberated by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and Yoga, having reached <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), remain like the unconscious, devoid of knowledge of the self and the supreme self.
But he has knowledge.
For he says:
Thus.
Acting in this way, the omniscient one makes known his freedom from delusion.
It has been said:
From all persons, both those stained by effect and instrument and those unstained,

children.text: aprāptāntaṃ puruṣaṃ yo 'bhyadhikaṃ varṇayet sa budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever describes the unsurpassed person, whose end has not been reached, as superior is wise.
He asks: what was to be reached has been reached.
Then is this merely a figurative expression?
The answer is: no.
Because of imperfect understanding, our tantra is not to be taken as confined to yogic completion.
Rather, even what is beyond that <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) is taught by the omniscient one.
Through vigilance one should reach the end of sufferings by the grace of <s>Īśa</s>.
Here the word pramāda indicates lack of attention toward what has not yet come, and also dependence on another.
Therefore this word apramāda, vigilance, should be understood as involving action to prevent future time, as in protecting a sprout.
Therefore one should remain disciplined and vigilant.
And for one who proceeds in that way, the lordly power of the <s>Māheśvara</s> is said to have already been attained.
In gacchet, 'one should go,' the going is attainment.
The roots gam and sṛp are in the sense of going.
The self is so called because it attains, as in the pallor of a leaf or the ripening of a fruit.
How?

children.text: tasminneva pravartato yo 'yaṃ duḥkhāpoho guṇastatreyaṃ gatiriti saṃjñā kriyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With regard to one acting in that very state, this removal of suffering which is a quality is given the designation 'going': this is the meaning.
In the phrase 'of sufferings,' the well-known sufferings are the internal, the physical or elemental, and the divine.

children.text: tatrādhyātmikaṃ dvividhaṃ duḥkhaṃ śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Among these, internal suffering is twofold: bodily and mental.

children.text: tatra manasi bhavaṃ mānasaṃ krodhalobhamohabhayaviṣāderṣyāsūyādveṣamadamānamātsaryāratyādyaviśeṣadarśanādinimittaṃ tad duḥkham ||
children.translated_text: There, mental suffering is what arises in the mind, caused by anger, greed, delusion, fear, poison, envy, spite, hatred, pride, arrogance, jealousy, dissatisfaction, non-discriminating perception, and the like.
Likewise there is bodily suffering, arising from causes such as headache, tooth disease, eye disease, fever, pratima, diarrhea, cough, asthma, abdominal illness, and the like.
And there is also another fivefold suffering.
Namely: gestation, birth, ignorance, old age, and death.

children.text: tatra garbhe tāvad yadāyaṃ puruṣo māturudare nyastagātraḥ khaṇḍaśakaṭastha iva pumān niyamaśramam anubhavamāno 'vakāśarahitaḥ ākuñcanaprasāraṇādiṣv aparyāptāvakāśaḥ sarvakriyāsu niruddha ityevam advārake andhatamasi mūḍho bandhanastha iva pumān avaśyaṃ samanubhavati ||
children.translated_text: In that regard, first, in the womb, when this <s>puruṣa</s> has his limbs placed in his mother's belly, like a man in a broken cart, experiencing the hardship of confinement, without space, with insufficient room for contracting, extending, and the like, restrained in all activity, thus bewildered in a doorless, pitch-dark place, like a man in bondage, he necessarily experiences suffering.
Why?

children.text: cetanatvād bhoktṛtvāt tanmayatvāc ca na tu kāryakaraṇāni ||
children.translated_text: Because he is conscious, because he is an experiencer, and because he is identified with it; but not the effects and instruments.
Why?
Because they are unconscious, because they are not experiencers, and because they are not identified with it.
Likewise there is also the suffering of birth.

children.text: yadāyaṃ puruṣo jāyamānaḥ purīṣapaṅkamagnavadano mūtradhārābhir abhiṣicyamāno dehe saṃvṛtadvārake yoniniḥsaraṇasaṃkaṭe 'tyarthaṃ pīḍyamāno 'sthimarmabandhanaiḥ praghṛṣyamāṇo vikrośan ninadaṃś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: When this <s>puruṣa</s>, being born, has his face sunk as if in a mire of excrement, is sprinkled by streams of urine, and, in the narrow passage out of the womb, whose openings are closed in the body, is extremely pressed, rubbed by the joints of bones and vital spots, crying out and making noise, he is born.

children.text: paścāt punastasyānucitena bāhyena vāyunā jananāvartena spṛṣṭasya tīvraṃ duḥkhamabhivyajyate ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, when he is touched by the unfamiliar external wind and by the turmoil of birth, intense suffering becomes manifest for him.
As in the case of royal pampered ones and the like.
And by that, the latent impression that is the cause of memory of other births and the like is lost for him.
Thus the suffering of birth is experienced by the <s>puruṣa</s> alone.
Why?
Because he is conscious, because he is an experiencer, and because he is identified with it.
But not the effects and instruments.
Why?
Because they are unconscious, because they are not experiencers, and because they are not identified with it.

children.text: tathā ajñānaduḥkhamapi ahaṃkārasatkṛtagātro na jānan ko 'haṃ kuto'haṃ kasyāhaṃ kena vā bandhanena baddho'hamiti kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kimakāraṇaṃ kiṃ bhakṣyaṃ kimabhakṣyaṃ kiṃ peyaṃ kimapeyaṃ kiṃ satyaṃ kimasatyaṃ kim jñānaṃ kimajñānam ityajñānaduḥkhaṃ puruṣa evānubhavati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the suffering of ignorance too: with his body honored by egoity, not knowing, 'Who am I? From where am I? Whose am I? By what bondage am I bound? What is cause? What is not cause? What may be eaten? What may not be eaten? What may be drunk? What may not be drunk? What is true? What is false? What is knowledge? What is ignorance?' the <s>puruṣa</s> alone experiences the suffering of ignorance.
Why?
Because he is conscious, because he is an experiencer, and because he is identified with it.
But not the effects and instruments.
Why?
Because they are unconscious, because they are not experiencers, and because they are not identified with it.
Likewise there is also the suffering of old age.

children.text: yadāyaṃ puruṣo jarājarjaritaḥ kṛśaśarīraḥ śithilīkṛtanayanakapolanāsikābhrūdaśanāvaraṇaḥ krauñcajānuriva nirviṇṇo 'kṣidūṣikādiṣvapakarṣaṇādiṣv asamartho vihaṃga iva lūnapakṣo laṅghanaplavanadhāvanādiṣv asamarthaḥ pūrvātītāni bhogavyāyāmaśilpakarmāṇy anusmaramāṇaḥ smṛtivaikalyam āpanno 'vaśyaṃ kleśamanubhavati ||
children.translated_text: When this <s>puruṣa</s>, worn down by old age, is thin-bodied, with eyes, cheeks, nose, brows, teeth, and covering loosened, dejected like a crane-kneed man, incapable of removing eye-filth and the like, like a bird with wings cut off, incapable of leaping, jumping, running, and so on, remembering former enjoyments, exercises, crafts, and works that have passed away, and afflicted by failure of memory, he necessarily experiences distress.
Why?
Because he is conscious, because he is an experiencer, and because he is identified with it.
But not the effects and instruments.
Why?
Because they are unconscious, because they are not experiencers, and because they are not identified with it.
Likewise there is also the suffering of death.

children.text: yadāyaṃ puruṣo maraṇasamaye ślathakaraṇaḥ śirodharam avalambamānaḥ śvāsanocchvasanatatparaḥ khurukhurāyamāṇakaṇṭhaḥ svopārjitamaṇikanakadhanadhānyapatnīputrapaśusaṃghātaḥ kasya bhaviṣyatīty anutapyamānaḥ viṣayānanu dodūyamānaḥ salilādi yācamāno viraktavadano marmabhiś chidyamānair avaśyaṃ kleśamanubhavati ||
children.translated_text: When this <s>puruṣa</s> at the time of death has slackened organs, his head and neck drooping, intent on breathing in and out, his throat rattling, grieving, 'To whom will the mass of jewels, gold, wealth, grain, wife, sons, and cattle acquired by me belong?', tormented after sense-objects, asking for water and the like, with a colorless face, and with his vital parts being cut, he necessarily experiences distress.
Why?
Because he is conscious, because he is an experiencer, and because he is identified with it.
But not the effects and instruments.
Why?
Because they are unconscious, because they are not experiencers, and because they are not identified with it.
For it has been said:

children.text: garbhe praviśan duḥkhaṃ nivasan duḥkhaṃ viniṣkraman duḥkham
children.translated_text: Entering the womb is suffering; dwelling there is suffering; coming out is suffering.
And once born, he meets suffering; therefore non-rebirth is better.
Thus.
Likewise there is also another fivefold suffering.

children.text: tadyathā ihalokabhayaṃ paralokabhayam ahitasaṃprayogaḥ hitaviprayogaḥ icchāvyāghātaśceti ||
children.translated_text: Namely: fear in this world, fear in the next world, union with what is harmful, separation from what is beneficial, and obstruction of desire.
Likewise there is also another threefold suffering.

children.text: ādhyātmikamajñānaṃ puruṣe ādhibhautikaṃ viṣayitvam ādhidaivikaṃ ca paśutvaṃ trividham aparaṃ prāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say that the other threefold suffering consists of internal ignorance in the <s>puruṣa</s>, the elemental condition of being an enjoyer of objects, and the divine condition of being a bound soul.
Things such as these are conventionally called sufferings because they are causes of birth, whose result is affliction and displeasure.

children.text: āha caraṇādhikāre 'natiprasādād aśivatvasaṃjñake sarvāṇy anatiprasādabījatvāt kuto nātyantanivṛttāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Someone says: In the section on practice, under the designation 'inauspiciousness' because of insufficient favor, why are all these not completely ceased, since they are all seeds of insufficient favor?
Why?

children.text: saṃhāraṃ prāptasya nigaḍamuktādhikāravan muktāv atiśayitaguṇaprāptyartham ucyate gacched duḥkhānāmantam ||
children.translated_text: It is said that, for one who has reached dissolution, as in the case of an office from which a fetter has been released, liberation is for the sake of attaining excellent qualities, and he would go to the end of sufferings.

children.text: duḥkhānām atyantaṃ paramāpoho guṇāvāptiśca paraṃ bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: The complete and supreme removal of sufferings and the attainment of qualities become supreme.
Both of these arise only from this.
Therefore he says: 'from the favor of <s>Īśa</s>.'
Here the word <s>Īśa</s> is a name of the Blessed One.
Why is he <s>Īśa</s>?
Because he rules over effects such as knowledge, he is <s>Īśa</s>.
Favor means the wish to bestow.

children.text: tasmāt prasādāt sarvaduḥkhāpoho guṇāvāptiś cadim upādhyantarāt paraparivādādivacanāt śuddhiriva yugapadityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, from that favor, the removal of all suffering and the attainment of qualities occur simultaneously, as purity does from another condition such as a statement of rejecting others; this is the meaning.
Thus this word atha is explained.

children.text: paśupater ityuddiṣṭayor duḥkhāntaprasādayor gacched duḥkhānām antamīśaprasādāditi duḥkhāntaṃ parisamāptamiti ||
children.translated_text: With regard to "of <s>Paśupati</s>": of the two things specified, the end of suffering and grace, one should reach the end of sufferings through the grace of the Lord; therefore the end of suffering has been completed.
Having thus completed the chapter, it is fitting to speak.
Thus.
Its meaning is the one stated before.
It is to be recited only by the rule, by the rule previously stated.
But not by the rule connected with the end of suffering, as in the case of <s>Gaṇapati</s>; this is the meaning.

children.text: āha kāmitvāt kṛpayā bhagavatā duḥkhānto dattaḥ svecchayaiva na punaraduḥkhāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He says: because he desires it, the Blessed Lord, out of compassion, has given the end of suffering by his own will, and he will not again make it into non-end-of-suffering.

children.text: athāśaktas tathāpyasya śaktivyāghātaḥ pācakavad akarmāpekṣatvaṃ cocyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, if he is powerless, even so the obstruction of his power, and his dependence on no action, like a cook, are stated.
Here we shall explain how the end of suffering is eternal.

children.text: yathā ca kāṅkṣato lipsataś ca sādhakādhikāranivṛttistathā vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we shall explain how, for one who longs and seeks, there is cessation of the sādhaka's qualification.
And this is stated for the purpose of concluding the topic.
Here, from ruling he is <s>Īśāna</s>.
Here the reason has been stated: "from ruling, he is <s>Īśāna</s>."
<s>Īśāna</s> means lord, master, and establisher.
He says: of what is he <s>Īśāna</s>?
That is stated: he is <s>Īśāna</s> of all.
The word "all" should be understood as denoting, without remainder, the category of vidyā.
He is <s>Īśāna</s> of the vidyās, which are directed toward dharma, artha, kāma, kaivalya, and their means; "of the vidyās" is genitive plural.

children.text: āha kiṃ vidyānāmeveśānaḥ na tu vidyābhirye vidanti ||
children.translated_text: He says: is he <s>Īśāna</s> only of the vidyās, and not of those who know through the vidyās?
It is stated.
Here, because of unsurpassed lordship, he is <s>Īśvara</s>.
Puruṣa means one endowed with consciousness.
He says: of what is he <s>Īśvara</s>?
That is stated: of all beings.

children.text: atra cetanācetaneṣu sarvaśabdaḥ na kevalaṃ pṛthivyādiṣu kiṃtu siddheśvaravarjaṃ cetaneṣveva sarvabhūtaprakṛterniravaśeṣavācī sarvaśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, with respect to sentient and insentient things, the word "all" is not to be understood only in regard to earth and the rest; rather, excluding the perfected lords, the word "all" should be understood as denoting without remainder the category of all beings precisely among sentient beings.
Why are they called beings?
Because they are caused to be, they are called beings; "of beings" is genitive plural.
He says: here some accept a <s>Brahmā</s> distinct from vidyā and beings.
Is he the lord of that one, or not?
It is stated: he is the lord.
Because he says so.

children.text: atra yo 'yaṃ viriñciḥ paramaḥ patiḥ sarvacetanavyatiriktaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ tasmin brahmasaṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: Here, this <s>Viriñci</s>, the supreme lord, the kṣetrajña distinct from all sentient beings, bears the designation <s>Brahmā</s>.
But not pradhāna and the rest.
Why?
Because that would contradict the expression "overlord."
And why is he <s>Brahmā</s>?
Because of expanding and because of greatness, he is <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: bṛṃhayate yasmād vidyākalābhūtāni bṛhac ca tebhya ityato 'dhipatirbrahmā ||
children.translated_text: Since he expands the vidyās, kalās, and beings, and since he is great in comparison with them, therefore <s>Brahmā</s> is the overlord.
"Of <s>Brahmā</s>" is genitive.
Adhi has the sense of presiding over.

children.text: tatsvābhāvyāt saṃhṛte cāsaṃhṛte ca kārya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because this is his nature, it applies to the effect both when withdrawn and when not withdrawn.
The lord of a lord is an overlord.
Like a king of kings.
Pati has the senses of protecting, seeing, and enjoying.
Because <s>Īśvara</s> protects <s>Brahmā</s> and the others.
He protects the effect beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
The overlord is <s>Brahmā</s>.
The overlord is <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bṛṃhayate yasmād vidyādikāryaṃ bṛhac ca tebhya ityato 'dhipatirbrahmā bhagavāniti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since he expands the effect beginning with vidyā, and since he is great in comparison with them, therefore the Blessed Lord is <s>Brahmā</s>, the overlord.

children.text: āha atra kāryakaraṇamahābhāgyam evātra brahmaṇi cintyate na tu sādhakasya lipsā lābho veti ||
children.translated_text: He says: here it is only the great fortune of the effect and cause that is considered in relation to <s>Brahmā</s>, not the sādhaka's desire or attainment.
It is stated: no.
Because he says so.

children.text: atra yeṣāṃ sādhikāratvād anatiprasannas teṣāmaśivatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāntaṃ gateṣu ca śivatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā āha śivo me astu iti ||
children.translated_text: Here, seeing that those who still have sādhaka-qualification are not fully favored and are in a non-Śiva state, and seeing the Śiva state in those who have reached the end of suffering, he says, "May <s>Śiva</s> be for me."
"For me" indicates the self and means "mine."
"May he be" expresses longing.
He longs, seeks, and searches; this is the meaning.

children.text: āha kiyantaṃ kālaṃ bhagavānasya śivo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He says: for how long is the Blessed Lord <s>Śiva</s> for him?
That is stated: eternally.
Because he says so.
Here, always means eternally, continuously, and without interruption.
He says: whom does he thus call?
Or who is <s>Śiva</s> for him?
It is stated.
Here, this word <s>Śiva</s> too is a name of the Blessed Lord.
Why is he <s>Śiva</s>?
Because he is completely full and completely satisfied, he is <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore, from the teaching "always <s>Śiva</s>," the end of suffering is eternal.
It is the cessation of qualification concerning the cause.
For that reason it is established that the end of suffering is eternal.

children.text: evamete pañca padārthāḥ kāryakāraṇayogavidhiduḥkhāntāḥ samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣopasaṃhāranigamanataś ca vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus these five categories, effect, cause, yoga, rule, and the end of suffering, have been explained through summary, expansion, division, specification, conclusion, and final statement.
For it has been said:

children.text: ādau yad bhavati samāsoktaṃ madhye tasya vistarataś ca vibhāgataś copanayanigamanena satāmapyeṣa niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What occurs at the beginning is stated in summary; in the middle there is its expansion and division. With application and conclusion, this is the ascertainment even for good people.
Thus.
Here first, the word pati is the instruction of the category of cause in summary.

children.text: vistarastu vāmo devo jyeṣṭho rudraḥ kāmaḥ śaṃkaraḥ kālaḥ kalavikaraṇo balavikaraṇo'ghoro ghorataraḥ sarvaḥ śarva tatpuruṣo mahādeva oṃkāra ṛṣir vipro mahānīśa īśāna īśvaro 'dhipatirbrahmā śiva ityevamādyo vistaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The expansion is as follows: <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Deva</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Kalavikaraṇa</s>, <s>Balavikaraṇa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Ghoratara</s>, <s>Sarva</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s>, <s>Ṛṣi</s>, <s>Vipra</s>, <s>Mahānīśa</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Adhipati</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and so on.

children.text: vibhāgo'pi anyat patitvam anyad ajātatvam anyad bhavodbhavatvamityādyo vibhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The division too is such as: lordship is one thing, unbornness another, and arising from existence another.

children.text: viśeṣaḥ anyeṣāṃ pradhānādīni asmākaṃ tadvyatirikto bhagavānīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The specification is: for others, pradhāna and the rest are the cause; for us, the Blessed <s>Īśvara</s> is distinct from them.
In the section on the cause, because he says, "<s>Īśvara</s> is of all beings."
This is the conclusion, and they call it pertaining to all desires.

children.text: nigamanam īśa īśāna īśvaro'dhipatirbrahmā śiva iti ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is: <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, ruler, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>.
Likewise, '<s>paśu</s>' is the introductory statement of the category called effect.
Its expansion is: <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>paśu</s>s.

children.text: utpādyā anugrāhyās tirobhāvyakālpyavikāryam aspadasya bodhyadhiṣṭheyatve cetyevam ādyaḥ sūtravidyādharmārthakāmair bhedair duḥkhāntaḥ vidyā ||
children.translated_text: What is to be produced, favored, concealed, fashioned, and modified, and the status of being the locus of what is to be known and established: things of this sort, with divisions such as sūtra, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, ending in the cessation of suffering, are <s>vidyā</s>.
<s>Kalā</s>s are twofold.
They are called effects and called instruments.
Among them, those called effects are earth and the rest.
Those called instruments are intellect and the rest.
And <s>paśu</s>s are threefold.
Gods, human beings, and animals.
Among them, the gods are eightfold, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
Humanity is of many kinds, beginning with brahmins.
Animal birth is fivefold, beginning with domestic animals and wild beasts.
<s>Paśu</s>s are also tainted and untainted.
Such and the like is the expansion.

children.text: vibhāgo'pi anyā vidyā anyāḥ kalāḥ anye ca paśava ityevamādyo vibhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The division too is as follows: <s>vidyā</s> is one thing, the <s>kalā</s>s are another, and the <s>paśu</s>s are others.

children.text: viśeṣaḥ anyeṣāṃ pradhānādīni kāraṇāni tānīha śāstre kāryatvena vyākhyātāni ||
children.translated_text: The particular distinction is this: what are causes for others, beginning with <s>pradhāna</s>, are explained in this śāstra as effects.

children.text: tatra pradhānaṃ kāraṇam anyeṣāṃ tadiha śāstre paśyanāt pāśakatvāt kāryatvena vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: Among them, <s>pradhāna</s> is a cause for others; in this śāstra it is explained as an effect because it is perceived and because it binds.

children.text: tathā puruṣaḥ kāraṇamanyatra iha śāstre paśutvāt kāryatvena vyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>puruṣa</s> is a cause elsewhere; in this śāstra, because it is a <s>paśu</s>, it is explained as an effect.
Likewise, because it stands in the midst of karma, time, and intrinsic nature, as in the case of withdrawal.
The elements are explained as effects because they are modifiable.
This is the particular distinction.
The summation means 'serving every desire'.
The conclusion is: <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and the beings or elements are <s>Brahman</s>.
Likewise, '<s>yoga</s>' is the introductory statement of the category <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: tasyaivaṃ carataḥ yogaḥ pravartate ubhayathā yaṣṭavyaḥ atyāgatiṃ gamayate nānyabhaktistu śaṃkare evaṃ devanityatānityayuktatā adhyayanaṃ dhyānaṃ smaraṇaṃ nityasāyujyamiti vistaraḥ vibhāgaḥ kriyālakṣaṇaṃ kriyoparamalakṣaṇaṃ dūradarśanaśravaṇamananavijñānāni gaṇapatiḥ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ sampravartate siddhaḥ gacched duḥkhānāmantam ityevamādyo vibhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who practices thus, <s>yoga</s> comes into operation; he is to worship in both ways; it brings him to the unsurpassed course; and devotion is to no other than <s>Śaṅkara</s>. Thus the expansion includes the god's permanence, connection with the permanent and impermanent, study, meditation, recollection, and eternal union. The division includes the mark of activity and the mark of cessation of activity, distant seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing, the lord of the gaṇas, and the fact that it mostly comes into operation. Having become perfected, he would go to the end of sufferings: such and the like is the division.
There are the power of knowledge and the power of action.
Among them, the power of knowledge consists in hearing and the rest.
The power of action consists in swiftness like that of the mind and the rest.
Such and the like is the division.

children.text: viśeṣaḥ anyeṣāṃ kaivalyam iha tu viśeṣo vikaraṇamiti ||
children.translated_text: The particular distinction is this: for others there is isolation; but here the special distinction is <s>vikaraṇa</s>.

children.text: pratikaraṇa iti kaivalyadharmātiśaktir niṣkalam aiśvaryamityeṣa viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for <s>pratikaraṇa</s>: the power that surpasses the dharma of isolation and the partless lordship; this is the particular distinction.
The summation is: 'endowed with these qualities'.

children.text: ato yāvanti vākyaviśeṣāṇi saṃnikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭāni nirvacanāni tāni ca sarvanirvacanānīti kṛtvā yuktamuktam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, however many particular statements there are, proximate or remote, and however many definitions there are, since these are all the definitions, what has been said is fitting and correct.

children.text: evamatra śrībhagavatkauṇḍinyaviracite śrīmadyogapāśupataśāstrasūtravyākhyāne pañcārthabhāṣye pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ saha brahmaṇā granthato 'rthataśca parisamāpta iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus here, in the venerable <s>Pañcārthabhāṣya</s>, the explanation of the sūtras of the venerable <s>Yogapāśupataśāstra</s> composed by the glorious blessed <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the fifth chapter, together with <s>Brahman</s>, is completely finished in both textual extent and meaning.
Auspiciousness.
